both, kept separate for regular and reserve service. The ABS says the ADF \"consists of regulars and reservists, and this variable provides a detailed breakdown of current and previous service for both\" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021), so it distinguishes a current regular who once served in the reserves from one who has only ever been a regular. ADFP on the same person row is the four-category collapse of the same answer, and both columns are new to the 2021 Census person table.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Australian Defence Force service, detailed (ADCP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/service-australian-defence-force/australian-defence-force-service-detailed-adcp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Australian defence force service detailed","t":"categorical","k":"Census Australian Defence Force service, detailed","def":"A single digit 1 to 8: four codes for people still serving (regular only, reserves only, and the two mixed histories), three for people who have left (regular only, reserves only, both), and 8 for never served. Not stated is '&', not applicable '@' and overseas visitor 'V'. Scope is persons aged 15 years and over.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Australian Defence Force service, detailed (ADCP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/service-australian-defence-force/australian-defence-force-service-detailed-adcp","lim":"It carries no rank, service branch, length of service, deployment or discharge date, so it cannot identify veterans by war service or by eligibility for Department of Veterans' Affairs support. It is a self-report at one Census night in August 2021 and there is no equivalent column on the 2011 or 2016 person tables, so a service history cannot be assembled across Censuses.","where":["madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"],"dom":0},{"n":"ADDIVD","d":"The river basin the dwelling sits in, coded from where the dwelling was enumerated.","full":"The river basin the dwelling sits in, coded from where the dwelling was enumerated. The ABS defines these divisions as \"an ABS Mesh Block approximation of drainage divisions provided through the Bureau of Meteorology's Australian Hydrological Geospatial Fabric\" (ASGS Edition 3), so this is a hydrological region rather than an administrative one. It sits with the other geography codes on the 2021 dwelling row - SA1UCD to SA4UCD, STEUCD, LGAD, POAD and CEDD - and is the one that places a dwelling in a catchment rather than in an administrative area.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Non ABS Structures, Australian Drainage Divisions","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/non-abs-structures/australian-drainage-divisions","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Australian drainage divisions (en)","k":"ASGS Australian Drainage Division code","def":"A three-character ASGS Non ABS Structure code: the letter D followed by a two-digit division number, for example D03 Murray-Darling Basin. There are 17 Australian Drainage Divisions covering the whole of Australia without gaps or overlaps, and that count already includes the three non-spatial special purpose codes D94 No usual address, D97 Migratory - Offshore - Shipping and DZZ Outside Australia. D91 Unclassified (Aust.) carries Christmas Island, the Cocos (Keeling) Islands and Norfolk Island.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Non ABS Structures, Australian Drainage Divisions","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/non-abs-structures/australian-drainage-divisions","lim":"A drainage division is not nested inside a state - the Murray-Darling Basin crosses four states and territories - so division totals and state totals are different groupings and the two cannot be treated as a hierarchy. Because the boundary is a Mesh Block approximation of the Geofabric rather than a surveyed catchment line, a dwelling close to a divide can be allocated to the neighbouring division.","where":["madipge-cen21-d-dwelling-2021 / census_2021_dwelling"]},{"n":"ADDIVP","d":"The river basin containing the person's usual address, coded from place of usual residence rather than from where they were counted on Census night.","full":"The river basin containing the person's usual address, coded from place of usual residence rather than from where they were counted on Census night. The ABS defines the divisions as \"an ABS Mesh Block approximation of drainage divisions provided through the Bureau of Meteorology's Australian Hydrological Geospatial Fabric\" (ASGS Edition 3). Where a person was away from home in August 2021 this can differ from ADDIVD on the dwelling record they were enumerated in, which is the enumeration-based coding of the same classification.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Non ABS Structures, Australian Drainage Divisions","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/non-abs-structures/australian-drainage-divisions","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Australian drainage divisions (ur)","k":"ASGS Australian Drainage Division code","def":"A three-character ASGS Non ABS Structure code: D followed by two digits, for example D03 Murray-Darling Basin. The 17 divisions cover the whole of Australia without gaps or overlaps and that count already includes the three non-spatial special purpose codes D94, D97 and DZZ; D91 Unclassified (Aust.) holds the Other Territories.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Non ABS Structures, Australian Drainage Divisions","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/non-abs-structures/australian-drainage-divisions","lim":"Living in a division does not mean drawing on its water, since most urban supply is piped across catchments, so this is a location code rather than a measure of exposure to a basin's water resources. It is also one snapshot of usual residence, so a move between divisions during the year leaves no trace here.","where":["madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"]},{"n":"ADFP","d":"Whether a person has ever served in the Australian Defence Force and, if so, whether they are still serving.","full":"Whether a person has ever served in the Australian Defence Force and, if so, whether they are still serving. The ABS says it \"describes whether a person is currently serving or has previously served in the Australian Defence Force (ADF)\" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021), covering the Army including NORFORCE, the Navy and the Air Force, and also National Service and the Second Australian Imperial Force. ADCP on the same row splits the same answer eight ways; this column is the four-way version used for headline veteran counts.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Australian Defence Force service (ADFP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/service-australian-defence-force/australian-defence-force-service-adfp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Australian defence force service","t":"categorical","k":"Census Australian Defence Force service","def":"Codes 1 currently serving in the regular service, 2 currently serving in the reserves, 3 not currently serving but has previously served, and 4 has never served, plus '&' not stated, '@' not applicable and 'V' overseas visitor. Scope is persons aged 15 years and over.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Australian Defence Force service (ADFP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/service-australian-defence-force/australian-defence-force-service-adfp","lim":"The four categories merge the mixed histories that ADCP keeps apart, so a current regular who once served in the reserves cannot be told from one who has only ever been a regular. Service in the ADF is all that counts, so police, emergency services and service in an allied country's military fall into 'has never served'.","where":["madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"],"dom":1},{"n":"AGE10P","d":"The person's age at Census night placed in ten-year bands, the coarsest of the three age columns on the 2021 person table.","full":"The person's age at Census night placed in ten-year bands, the coarsest of the three age columns on the 2021 person table. The ABS says it \"collects each person's age in ten-year groups. If age is not reported, it is imputed\" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021), so the bands are built from the same reported date of birth or stated age that AGEP holds in single years. AGE5P sits between the two at five-year bands.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Age in ten year groups (AGE10P)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/age-ten-year-groups-age10p","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Age in ten year groups","t":"categorical","k":"Census age in ten-year groups","def":"Eleven codes, 01 for 0-9 years through 10 for 90-99 years, with 11 for 100 years and over. There is no not stated category, because an unreported age is imputed rather than left blank.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Age in ten year groups (AGE10P)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/age-ten-year-groups-age10p","lim":"The bands cut across the ages that decide eligibility and scope - 15, 16, 18, 25 and 65 all fall inside a band - so labour force scope, income support eligibility or pension age cannot be worked out from this column. Use AGEP where a threshold matters, and note that a mean age from banded data depends on the midpoint assumed for the open top group.","where":["madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"],"dom":2},{"n":"AGE5P","d":"The person's age at Census night placed in five-year bands, the age column used for standard population pyramids and for age-standardising Census counts.","full":"The person's age at Census night placed in five-year bands, the age column used for standard population pyramids and for age-standardising Census counts. The ABS says it \"collects each person's age in five-year groups. If age is not reported, it is imputed\" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). It is derived from the same answer as AGEP, so it never disagrees with the single-year column, and AGE10P is the coarser version of it.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Age in five year groups (AGE5P)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/age-five-year-groups-age5p","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Age in 5-year groups","t":"categorical","k":"Census age in five-year groups","def":"Twenty-one groups running from 0-4 years to 100 years and over. Imputed ages are included in the bands, so there is no not stated code.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Age in five year groups (AGE5P)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/age-five-year-groups-age5p","lim":"Five-year bands still straddle the ages that decide scope: 16, 18 and 21 all sit inside the 15-19 and 20-24 bands, so a school-leaving, voting or drinking-age population cannot be built here. The top group is open, so it cannot separate the very old and any mean age depends on the midpoint chosen for it.","where":["madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"],"dom":3},{"n":"AGEP","d":"Age in completed years at Census night, and the age column to use whenever an analysis needs an exact threshold.","full":"Age in completed years at Census night, and the age column to use whenever an analysis needs an exact threshold. The ABS says it \"collects each person's age. If age is not reported, it is imputed\" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021); age is derived from date of birth where that was given and from stated age otherwise. It appears on the 2011, 2016 and 2021 person tables, so it is the one demographic column that supports the same cut across all three Censuses, and IFAGEP, which sits on all three of those person tables, flags which records were imputed.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Age (AGEP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/age-agep","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Age of respondent","t":"categorical","k":"Census age in completed years","def":"Whole years from 0 to 115, with 0 recorded for infants aged less than one year. Age is output in whole years only, so there are no months or fractions and no not stated code.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Age (AGEP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/age-agep","lim":"A missing age is filled in rather than flagged in this column - IFAGEP is the flag - so a record with an age is not necessarily a record where age was reported. Imputation reached 4.4% of persons nationally in 2021 and more than 20% in some remote communities, which means an age distribution for a small area can be partly modelled rather than reported.","where":["madip-ge-030101d-census2016-census2016person-2016 / census_2016_person","madipge-cen11-d-person-2011 / census_2011_person","madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"],"dom":4},{"n":"ANC1P","d":"The first of up to two ancestries a person reported, coded to the ABS cultural and ethnic groups classification.","full":"The first of up to two ancestries a person reported, coded to the ABS cultural and ethnic groups classification. The ABS says the variable \"indicates how a person identifies their ancestry. Respondents are able to provide up to two responses. The first ancestry provided is output into Ancestry 1st response (ANC1P)\" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). ANC2P holds the second response and ANCRP says how many were given; ancestry is asked of everyone and is a separate question from country of birth in BPLP and from Indigenous status in INGP.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Ancestry 1st response (ANC1P)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/ancestry-1st-response-anc1p","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Ancestry 1st Response","t":"categorical","k":"ASCCEG 2019 cultural and ethnic group code","def":"A code from the Australian Standard Classification of Cultural and Ethnic Groups (ASCCEG), 2019: 321 categories at the four-digit level, 41 at two digits and 12 at one digit, with supplementary codes for inadequately described, not stated (&&&&) and overseas visitor (VVVV).","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Ancestry 1st response (ANC1P)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/ancestry-1st-response-anc1p","lim":"First and second are processing order, not preference, so treating ANC1P as a person's main or strongest ancestry overstates what was asked. Only two responses are kept, so a person identifying with three or more has the rest dropped, and the 6.2% non-response in 2021 falls into the not stated code rather than being spread across groups.","where":["madip-ge-030101d-census2016-census2016person-2016 / census_2016_person","madipge-cen11-d-person-2011 / census_2011_person","madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"],"dom":5},{"n":"ANC2P","d":"The second ancestry a person reported, populated only for the people who gave two.","full":"The second ancestry a person reported, populated only for the people who gave two. The ABS says \"the second ancestry provided is output into Ancestry 2nd response (ANC2P)\" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021), using the same classification as ANC1P. Because a person who reported one ancestry is coded not applicable here rather than not stated, this column is what distinguishes single-ancestry identification from a missing answer.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Ancestry 2nd response (ANC2P)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/ancestry-2nd-response-anc2p","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Ancestry 2nd Response","t":"categorical","k":"ASCCEG 2019 cultural and ethnic group code","def":"The same ASCCEG 2019 codes as ANC1P, with 321 four-digit categories. There is no not stated category: a person who gave one ancestry is coded not applicable, and a person who answered nothing appears as not stated in ANC1P.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Ancestry 2nd response (ANC2P)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/ancestry-2nd-response-anc2p","lim":"Not applicable is not proof of a single ancestry - it means only one was written down, and the form accepts at most two, so the column cannot measure how many ancestries a person actually claims. Adding counts from ANC1P and ANC2P also double-counts people rather than ancestries unless the responses are combined, which is what the ABS variable ANCP does; the PLIDA Census tables do not carry ANCP.","where":["madip-ge-030101d-census2016-census2016person-2016 / census_2016_person","madipge-cen11-d-person-2011 / census_2011_person","madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"],"dom":6},{"n":"ANCRP","d":"Whether the person gave one ancestry or two, held as a count rather than as the ancestries themselves.","full":"Whether the person gave one ancestry or two, held as a count rather than as the ancestries themselves. It saves a user from having to infer multiple identification by testing whether ANC2P is not applicable, and it is on the 2021 person table only.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Ancestry one or two response indicator (ANCRP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/ancestry-one-or-two-response-indicator-ancrp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Ancestry one or two response indicator","t":"categorical","k":"Census ancestry response count indicator","def":"Codes 1 one response and 2 two responses, plus '&' not stated and 'V' overseas visitor.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Ancestry one or two response indicator (ANCRP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/ancestry-one-or-two-response-indicator-ancrp","lim":"It counts what was written down, not what a person identifies with: the form takes at most two ancestries, so a person with three is coded the same as a person with exactly two. It exists only for 2021, so the same measure of multiple ancestry cannot be made on the 2011 or 2016 person tables.","where":["madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"],"dom":7},{"n":"ASSNP","d":"Whether the person needs help with self-care, mobility or communication because of a long-term condition, a disability or old age - the Census's proxy for profound or severe disability.","full":"Whether the person needs help with self-care, mobility or communication because of a long-term condition, a disability or old age - the Census's proxy for profound or severe disability. The ABS says it \"records the number of people with a profound or severe core activity limitation\", who are \"those needing assistance in their day to day lives in one or more of the three core activity areas of self-care, mobility and communication\" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). It is on the 2011, 2016 and 2021 person tables, which makes it the only measure of a person's own disability in the Census that spans all three.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Core activity need for assistance (ASSNP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/disability-and-carers/core-activity-need-assistance-assnp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Core Activity Need for Assistance","t":"categorical","k":"Census core activity need for assistance","def":"Codes 1 has need for assistance with core activities and 2 does not, plus '&' not stated and 'V' overseas visitor. There is no not applicable code, because the question is asked of all persons.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Core activity need for assistance (ASSNP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/disability-and-carers/core-activity-need-assistance-assnp","lim":"It is a threshold and not a scale: it finds the profound and severe end only, so people with a moderate or mild limitation, and people who need help with tasks outside self-care, mobility and communication, are coded as having no need. The ABS defines place of usual residence as \"the geographic area in which a person usually lives. It may or may not be the place where the person was counted on Census Night\" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021), and AUSTP is the Australia (AUS) level of that coding, the coarsest of the geography columns on the 2021 person table alongside STEUCP, SA4UCP down to MBUCP for the same address. Its practical job is to isolate the overseas visitor, no usual address and migratory, off-shore and shipping cases before any finer geography is analysed.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence (PURP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-usual-residence-purp","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Australia (ur)","k":"ASGS Australia (AUS) level of place of usual residence","def":"The Australia (AUS) level of the ASGS Main Structure, the top of the hierarchy that Mesh Blocks, SA1s to SA4s and states and territories aggregate into, together with the extra categories the usual residence coding carries: no usual address, migratory, off-shore and shipping, and overseas visitor (VVVV). There is no not stated code: an incomplete usual address is imputed, and IFPURP records that it was.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence (PURP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-usual-residence-purp","lim":"Being the top of the hierarchy, it separates almost nobody: nearly every person counted has a usual address in Australia, so a cross-tabulation on this column alone will look empty. It also records the address as at Census night 2021, not a residency test, so a person on a short overseas posting who kept an Australian usual address is coded in Australia.","where":["madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"]},{"n":"AUSTU1P","d":"Whether the person's usual address one year before the Census was in Australia.","full":"Whether the person's usual address one year before the Census was in Australia. The ABS defines the underlying concept as \"the geographic area in which a person usually lived one year before the Census\" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021), and this column is the Australia (AUS) level of that coding, with AUSTU5P doing the same job for five years earlier. Read against AUSTP it is what identifies people who arrived from overseas in the year to August 2021.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence one year ago (PUR1P)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-usual-residence-one-year-ago-pur1p","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Australia (ur1y)","k":"ASGS Australia (AUS) level of place of usual residence one year ago","def":"The Australia (AUS) level of the ASGS coding of place of usual residence one year ago, so in practice a split between in Australia and the overseas category the ABS codes at 9299 in the SA2-level output, with not stated for people who did not answer and not applicable for children under one year.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence one year ago (PUR1P)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-usual-residence-one-year-ago-pur1p","lim":"It compares two points and nothing in between, so a person who went overseas and came back within the year is coded exactly like a person who never left, and there is no arrival date. Non-response was 6.0% in 2021, which is large relative to the overseas group this column is usually used to find.","where":["madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"]},{"n":"AUSTU5P","d":"Whether the person's usual address five years before the Census was in Australia.","full":"Whether the person's usual address five years before the Census was in Australia. The ABS defines the concept as \"the geographic area in which a person usually lived five years before the Census\" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021), which for the 2021 Census means the position at 10 August 2016. It is the coarsest of the five-year mobility columns on the person table, sitting above STEU5P, LGAU5P and MBU5P for the same address.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence five years ago (PUR5P)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-usual-residence-five-years-ago-pur5p","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Australia (ur5y)","k":"ASGS Australia (AUS) level of place of usual residence five years ago","def":"The Australia (AUS) level of the ASGS coding of place of usual residence five years ago, giving an in Australia against overseas split, with additional categories for no usual residence, migratory, off-shore and shipping, not stated, and not applicable.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence five years ago (PUR5P)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-usual-residence-five-years-ago-pur5p","lim":"Scope is persons aged five years and over, so every younger child is not applicable and cannot be counted as a mover or an arrival. The five-year gap hides everything between the two dates: someone who spent four of those years overseas and returned before Census night is coded the same as someone who never left. Non-response was 6.9% in 2021.","where":["madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"]},{"n":"BEDD","d":"The number of bedrooms in the occupied private dwelling, held as a number rather than as a range.","full":"The number of bedrooms in the occupied private dwelling, held as a number rather than as a range. The ABS says it \"records the count of bedrooms in each occupied private dwelling\" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021), and the form asks respondents to include any room built as a bedroom even where it is now a study, office, computer room or sewing room. BEDRD on the same dwelling row is the banded version, and this column is one of the inputs to housing suitability (HOSD) on that row.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Number of bedrooms in private dwelling (BEDD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/number-bedrooms-private-dwelling-bedd","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Number of Bedrooms in Private Dwelling","t":"categorical","k":"Census count of bedrooms in an occupied private dwelling","def":"Two digits: 00 for none, which includes studio apartments and bedsitters, through 29, with 30 meaning 30 or more bedrooms. Not stated is '&&' and not applicable '@@'.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Number of bedrooms in private dwelling (BEDD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/number-bedrooms-private-dwelling-bedd","lim":"It counts the dwelling's rooms, not how the household uses them, so it cannot say how many people sleep in a room or whether a household is crowded - HOSD combines it with household composition to answer that. Unoccupied private dwellings and all non-private dwellings are not applicable, so a bedroom count is missing precisely where institutional and group living is.","where":["madip-ge-030103d-census2016-census2016dwelling-2016 / census_2016_dwelling","madipge-cen11-d-dwelling-2011 / census_2011_dwelling","madipge-cen21-d-dwelling-2021 / census_2021_dwelling"],"dom":9},{"n":"BEDRD","d":"The dwelling's bedroom count collapsed into seven groups, topping out at six or more.","full":"The dwelling's bedroom count collapsed into seven groups, topping out at six or more. The ABS says it \"records the number of bedrooms in each occupied private dwelling in ranges\" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). It is a recode of BEDD on the same row, so the two never disagree, and it is the version used in most published Census housing tables.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Number of bedrooms in private dwelling (ranges) (BEDRD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/number-bedrooms-private-dwelling-ranges-bedrd","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Number of Bedrooms in Private Dwelling (ranges)","t":"categorical","k":"Census count of bedrooms in an occupied private dwelling, in ranges","def":"A single digit: 0 none, which includes studio apartments and bedsitters, 1 through 5 for one to five bedrooms, and 6 for six bedrooms or more. Not stated is '&' and not applicable '@', the latter covering unoccupied private dwellings, non-private dwellings and migratory, off-shore and shipping SA1s.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Number of bedrooms in private dwelling (ranges) (BEDRD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/number-bedrooms-private-dwelling-ranges-bedrd","lim":"The open top group means large dwellings cannot be separated and any mean bedroom count from this column is biased down. It is not an independent measurement either: because it is derived from BEDD, using both columns adds no information and cannot be used to cross-check the answer.","where":["madip-ge-030103d-census2016-census2016dwelling-2016 / census_2016_dwelling","madipge-cen11-d-dwelling-2011 / census_2011_dwelling","madipge-cen21-d-dwelling-2021 / census_2021_dwelling"],"dom":10},{"n":"BPFP","d":"The country the person's mother was born in, as reported on the person's own Census form.","full":"The country the person's mother was born in, as reported on the person's own Census form. The ABS says it \"indicates the country in which a person's mother was born\" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). With BPMP for the father it feeds the derived summary BPPP, and together with BPLP it is what identifies second-generation Australians.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Country of birth of mother (BPFP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/country-birth-mother-bpfp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Country of Birth of Mother","t":"categorical","k":"SACC 2016 country code, mother's country of birth","def":"A four-digit Standard Australian Classification of Countries (SACC), 2016 code, 293 categories grouped into nine regions such as Oceania and Antarctica and South-East Asia, with supplementary codes 0000 inadequately described and 0001 at sea, '&&&&' not stated and 'VVVV' overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Country of birth of mother (BPFP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/country-birth-mother-bpfp","lim":"It is a birthplace reported on the respondent's form, not a link to the mother's own Census record, so it can be unknown or wrong where the respondent did not grow up with her - the 2021 non-response rate was 5.6%. It sits on the person table with YARP year of arrival, CITP citizenship and LANP language used at home, and those companions are what turn a birthplace into a migration history.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Country of birth of person (BPLP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/country-birth-person-bplp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Country of Birth of Person","t":"categorical","k":"SACC 2016 country of birth code","def":"A Standard Australian Classification of Countries (SACC), 2016 code with 293 categories at the four-digit level, 39 at two digits and 12 at one digit, plus supplementary codes for inadequately described, at sea, not stated and overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Country of birth of person (BPLP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/country-birth-person-bplp","lim":"Country of birth is neither migration status nor ancestry: an Australian citizen born overseas, a temporary visa holder and a permanent migrant share the same code, and only CITP, YARP or linked visa data separate them. Non-response was 5.3% in 2021.","where":["madip-ge-030101d-census2016-census2016person-2016 / census_2016_person","madipge-cen11-d-person-2011 / census_2011_person","madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"],"dom":12},{"n":"BPMP","d":"The country the person's father was born in, carried under the older PLIDA label 'Birthplace of Male Parent'.","full":"The country the person's father was born in, carried under the older PLIDA label 'Birthplace of Male Parent'. The ABS says it \"indicates the country of birth of each person's father\" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021), and the 2021 Census Dictionary now names it country of birth of father. It is the companion to BPFP for the mother, and the two are the only inputs to the derived generational summary BPPP.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Country of birth of father (BPMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/country-birth-father-bpmp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Birthplace of Male Parent","t":"categorical","k":"SACC 2016 country code, father's country of birth","def":"A four-digit Standard Australian Classification of Countries (SACC), 2016 code with 293 categories across nine regions, plus 0000 inadequately described, 0001 at sea, '&&&&' not stated and 'VVVV' overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Country of birth of father (BPMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/country-birth-father-bpmp","lim":"A not stated father's birthplace pushes the whole record into the not stated category of BPPP, so the 5.7% non-response here propagates into any first- or second-generation Australian count built from that derived column. The ABS says it \"indicates if a person's father and/or mother was born in Australia or overseas\" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). It is derived from BPFP and BPMP on the same row and is the column that supports first- and second-generation Australian analysis once it is crossed with the person's own country of birth in BPLP.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Country of birth of parents (BPPP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/country-birth-parents-bppp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Country of Birth of Parents","t":"categorical","k":"Census country of birth of parents summary","def":"Six categories: both parents born overseas, father only born overseas, mother only born overseas, both parents born in Australia, not stated where the birthplace of either or both parents was not stated, and overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Country of birth of parents (BPPP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/country-birth-parents-bppp","lim":"It collapses everything to Australia against overseas, so it cannot say which country a parent came from - BPFP and BPMP are needed for that. It is also not generational status on its own: an Australian-born person with an overseas-born parent is second generation, but an overseas-born person with the same parents is first, and only BPLP tells them apart.","where":["madip-ge-030101d-census2016-census2016person-2016 / census_2016_person","madipge-cen11-d-person-2011 / census_2011_person","madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"],"dom":14},{"n":"C11_PERSON_ID","d":"The key that ties a 2011 Census person record to the family and dwelling records collected with it.","full":"The key that ties a 2011 Census person record to the family and dwelling records collected with it. All three 2011 Census tables carry it, which is why a person identifier appears on tables that otherwise look like family and dwelling tables: a person's own characteristics, their family's composition and their dwelling's attributes all join on this column. It is an identifier created for the integrated asset, which the ABS describes as \"a secure data asset combining information on health, education, government payments, income and taxation, employment, and population demographics (including the Census) over time\", and links out to other PLIDA sources run through the person linkage spine rather than through this column. The 2016 Census tables and the 2021 person table carry SYNTHETIC_AEUID as the person key in its place, while DWELLING_ID and FAMILY_ID - which are on the 2011 tables as well - are the dwelling and family keys.","dsrc":"ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/data-integration/integrated-data/person-level-integrated-data-asset-plida","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Synthetic Census 2011 person ID","k":"Synthetic 2011 Census person identifier","def":"An opaque identifier with no internal meaning: it does not encode a name, a date of birth or a location, and there is no finite list to publish.","p":"2011","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/data-integration/integrated-data/person-level-integrated-data-asset-plida","lim":"It is unique within the 2011 Census only. It does not carry across to the 2016 or 2021 Census tables and it is not the spine identifier, so a person cannot be followed between Censuses on this column - the spine link is what does that. The ABS says it \"indicates whether a person has attained a Certificate III or higher or is currently studying a non-school qualification\" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). It includes up to three children who were temporarily absent from the household on Census Night\" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). It is the total that CDCF, CDCUF, CDSF and CNDCF break apart by dependency, and unlike them it does not encode family type in the code.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of all children in family (CACF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/count-all-children-family-cacf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Count of All Children in Family","t":"categorical","k":"Census count of all children in a family","def":"Codes 1 to 5 for one to five children and 6 for six or more, plus '@' not applicable. CCLTHD is the same count for children under 15 and CPLTHD covers everyone, so the three together give the household's illness profile by age group; the person-level counterpart is CLTHP.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of adults (15 years and over) with selected long-term health condition(s) in household (CALTHD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/health/count-adults-15-years-and-over-selected-long-term-health-conditions-household-calthd","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Count of adults (15 years and over) with selected long-term health condition(s) in household","t":"categorical","k":"Census count of adults with a selected long-term health condition in the household","def":"A single digit: 0 to 4 for no adults through four adults, 5 for five or more, and 6 where some adults in the household did not state a condition. The answer comes from the persons temporarily absent question on the household form, and those same children are already included in the family totals CDCF, CDCUF and CACF.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of dependent children under 15 in family temporarily absent (CDCAF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/count-dependent-children-under-15-family-temporarily-absent-cdcaf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Count of Dependent Children Under 15 Temporarily Absent","t":"categorical","k":"Census count of dependent children under 15 temporarily absent from the family","def":"Codes 0 to 3, since at most three people can be reported as temporarily absent from a dwelling, plus '@' not applicable for families with no children under 15 and for non-family, unoccupied and non-private dwellings.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of dependent children under 15 in family temporarily absent (CDCAF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/count-dependent-children-under-15-family-temporarily-absent-cdcaf","lim":"The cap is three people per dwelling and it is shared with CDSAF and CNDAF, so a family with several members away on Census night has its absences truncated and the family counts understated. With CDCUF for the under-15s it makes up the dependent child total in CDCF.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of dependent students (15-24 years) in family (CDSF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/count-dependent-students-15-24-years-family-cdsf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Count of dependent students (15-24 years) in family","t":"categorical","k":"Census count of dependent students aged 15-24 in a family, by family type","def":"Two digits: 00 to 06 for couple families with no dependent students through six or more, 07 to 13 for one parent families over the same range, and '@@' not applicable. It sits with SEDD and SED22D for state electorates and with LGAD, POAD and SALD on the same dwelling row.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Non ABS Structures, Commonwealth Electoral Divisions","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/non-abs-structures/commonwealth-electoral-divisions","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Commonwealth electoral divisions (en)","k":"ASGS Commonwealth Electoral Division code","def":"A three-digit ASGS Non ABS Structure code: one digit for the state or territory and two for the division, assigned alphabetically within each state and territory. The ABS builds the divisions as \"an ABS Mesh Block approximation of Australian Electoral Commission (AEC) federal electoral divisions\" (ASGS Edition 3). Because it is coded from place of usual residence, it can differ from CEDD on the dwelling record a person was enumerated in, and it is the column to use for describing an electorate's resident population.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Non ABS Structures, Commonwealth Electoral Divisions","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/non-abs-structures/commonwealth-electoral-divisions","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Commonwealth electoral divisions (ur)","k":"ASGS Commonwealth Electoral Division code","def":"A three-digit ASGS Non ABS Structure code, one digit for state or territory and two for the division, over the 169 divisions that cover Australia in ASGS Edition 3, a count that includes 19 non-spatial special purpose codes.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Non ABS Structures, Commonwealth Electoral Divisions","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/non-abs-structures/commonwealth-electoral-divisions","lim":"The people counted in a division are not its voters: children, non-citizens and adults who are not enrolled are all included, so a Census population is a poor proxy for enrolment or for turnout. The ABS says it \"records people who, in the two weeks prior to Census Night, spent time caring for a child or children aged under 15 years without pay\" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). It covers care of a person's own children whether or not they live together, and of grandchildren, relatives' children and friends' or neighbours' children, but not organised care through an institution or club. The ABS says the variable \"records whether a person has Australian citizenship\" and that the data \"is used to understand the tendency of different migrant groups to take up citizenship and to measure the size of the groups eligible to vote\" (ABS Census Dictionary 2021). It is asked of everyone and is on the 2011, 2016 and 2021 person tables, so with BPLP and YARP it supports a take-up-of-citizenship analysis across three Censuses.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Australian citizenship (CITP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/australian-citizenship-citp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Australian Citizenship","t":"categorical","k":"Census Australian citizenship indicator","def":"Codes 1 Australian citizen and 2 not an Australian citizen, plus '&' not stated and 'V' overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Australian citizenship (CITP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/cultural-diversity/australian-citizenship-citp","lim":"It is self-reported and not checked against the citizenship register, and it says nothing about what a non-citizen holds instead: permanent residence, a temporary visa and no visa at all share the single code 2. It is derived from the individual condition flags HARTP, HASTP, HCANP, HDEMP, HDIAP, HHEDP, HKIDP, HLUNP, HMHCP and HSTRP on the same person row, and it is the person-level counterpart to the household counts CALTHD, CCLTHD and CPLTHD.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of selected long-term health conditions (CLTHP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/health/count-selected-long-term-health-conditions-cthp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Count of selected long-term health conditions","t":"categorical","k":"Census count of selected long-term health conditions","def":"Codes 0 none of the selected conditions, 1 one, 2 two and 3 three or more, plus '&' not stated and 'V' overseas visitor. These people are adult children still usually resident with a parent, and they are already included in CNDCF and CACF.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of non-dependent children in family temporarily absent (CNDAF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/count-non-dependent-children-family-temporarily-absent-cndaf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Count of Non-Dependent Children Temporarily Absent","t":"categorical","k":"Census count of non-dependent children temporarily absent from the family","def":"Codes 0 to 3, plus '@' not applicable, which covers families with no non-dependent children as well as non-family households, unoccupied private dwellings and non-private dwellings.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of non-dependent children in family temporarily absent (CNDAF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/count-non-dependent-children-family-temporarily-absent-cndaf","lim":"The three-person cap applies to the dwelling as a whole, so this count competes with CDCAF and CDSAF rather than adding to them, and a dwelling with several members away has its absences truncated. It is the residual of CACF once the dependent children in CDCF are removed, and it includes up to three non-dependent children temporarily absent on Census night.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of non-dependent children in family (CNDCF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/count-non-dependent-children-family-cndcf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Count of Non-Dependent Children in Family","t":"categorical","k":"Census count of non-dependent children in a family, by family type","def":"Two digits: 00 to 06 for couple families with no non-dependent children through six or more, 07 to 13 for one parent families over the same range, and '@@' not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of non-dependent children in family (CNDCF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/count-non-dependent-children-family-cndcf","lim":"The status is fragile by construction: as soon as an adult child's own partner or child moves in, they stop being a non-dependent child and the family is reclassified, so a fall in this count can mean a household re-formed rather than a child leaving home. It is derived from HARTP and HASTP on the same row and is one of twelve pre-built comorbidity pairs new to the 2021 person table; a person is coded 1 whatever else they reported.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has arthritis and asthma (COARASP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/health/whether-has-arthritis-and-asthma-coarasp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Whether has arthritis and asthma","t":"categorical","k":"Census comorbidity indicator, arthritis and asthma","def":"Codes 1 has arthritis and asthma and 2 does not have arthritis and asthma, plus '&' not stated and 'V' overseas visitor.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has arthritis and asthma (COARASP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/health/whether-has-arthritis-and-asthma-coarasp","lim":"Code 2 lumps together people with neither condition, people with arthritis only and people with asthma only, so it is not a comparison group - HARTP and HASTP are needed to separate them. It is derived from HARTP and HHEDP on the same row, and the person is coded 1 regardless of any other conditions they reported.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has arthritis and heart disease (COARHDP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/health/whether-has-arthritis-and-heart-disease-coarhdp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Whether has arthritis and heart disease","t":"categorical","k":"Census comorbidity indicator, arthritis and heart disease","def":"Codes 1 has arthritis and heart disease and 2 does not, plus '&' not stated and 'V' overseas visitor.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has arthritis and heart disease (COARHDP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/health/whether-has-arthritis-and-heart-disease-coarhdp","lim":"The heart disease tick covers a heart attack decades ago and continuing angina equally, and there is no date of onset for either condition, so the column is a prevalence snapshot at August 2021 and cannot support any sequence or incidence analysis. It is derived from HASTP and HHEDP on the same person row.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has asthma and heart disease (COASHDP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/health/whether-has-asthma-and-heart-disease-coashdp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Whether has asthma and heart disease","t":"categorical","k":"Census comorbidity indicator, asthma and heart disease","def":"Codes 1 has asthma and heart disease and 2 does not, plus '&' not stated and 'V' overseas visitor.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has asthma and heart disease (COASHDP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/health/whether-has-asthma-and-heart-disease-coashdp","lim":"Breathlessness is a symptom of both conditions, and the Census has no clinical confirmation, so a code of 1 can reflect one underlying illness described two ways. It is derived from HASTP and HLUNP on the same row, and it is the one comorbidity pair in the set where the two conditions affect the same organ system.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has asthma and lung condition (COASLCP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/health/whether-has-asthma-and-lung-condition-coaslcp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Whether has asthma and lung condition","t":"categorical","k":"Census comorbidity indicator, asthma and lung condition","def":"Codes 1 has asthma and lung condition and 2 does not, plus '&' not stated and 'V' overseas visitor.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has asthma and lung condition (COASLCP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/health/whether-has-asthma-and-lung-condition-coaslcp","lim":"Asthma and COPD overlap clinically and are hard for a respondent to tell apart, so a code of 1 may be one condition reported twice rather than two distinct diseases. ABS defines it as describing \"whether a person has reported having both cancer (including remission) and heart disease (including heart attack or angina)\". It is a pre-computed cross of the two single-condition columns HCANP and HHEDP that sit on the same person row, published so a common pairing can be counted without building it. Asthma is a separate tick on the form and a separate column, HASTP, so it does not feed this pairing.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has lung condition and mental health condition (COLCMHP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/health/whether-has-lung-condition-and-mental-health-condition-colcmhp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Whether has lung condition and mental health condition","t":"categorical","k":"Census comorbidity flag (has both named conditions, or not)","def":"A single character: 1 has both conditions, 2 does not have both, & not stated, V overseas visitor.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has lung condition and mental health condition (COLCMHP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/health/whether-has-lung-condition-and-mental-health-condition-colcmhp","lim":"A person with asthma and depression is coded 2 here, not 1, because asthma is counted as its own condition and the asthma-with-mental-health pairing has no pre-computed column. ABS defines it as counting \"the total number of people who were reported as temporarily absent from the household\", taken from the persons temporarily absent block of the Census form. ABS defines it as counting \"the total number of people who were temporarily absent from a family on Census Night\", and processing counts partners, children and grandchildren under 15 who belong to the family structure while excluding other absent household members. It sits beside CALTHD and CCLTHD, which split the same count into adults aged 15 and over and children, and beside CPLTHRD, the ranged version. It is a headcount of affected people, not of conditions, so a person reporting four conditions adds one to the total.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of persons with selected long-term health condition(s) in household (CPLTHD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/health/count-persons-selected-long-term-health-conditions-household-cplthd","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Count of persons with selected long-term health condition(s) in household","t":"categorical","k":"Count of household members with at least one selected long-term health condition (00 to 10)","def":"Two characters. 00 to 10 count zero through ten or more affected persons, 11 marks a household where some members left the health question blank, && where all members did, and @@ not applicable.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of persons with selected long-term health condition(s) in household (CPLTHD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/health/count-persons-selected-long-term-health-conditions-household-cplthd","lim":"It does not say which conditions are present or who has them, so a household with one person with dementia and a household with one person with asthma are indistinguishable. ABS defines it as counting \"the number of people in a household who reported they had at least one of the selected long-term health conditions in ranges\", over the same ten conditions used by CPLTHD. It is built from relationship in household (RLHP) and the count of persons temporarily absent (CPAF), so up to three absent members are counted in the total. The column appears in the 2011, 2016 and 2021 family tables.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Count of persons in family (CPRF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/count-persons-family-cprf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Count of Persons in Family","t":"categorical","k":"Count of persons in the family (2 to 6 or more)","def":"A single digit, 2 to 6, where 6 means six or more persons, with @ for not applicable. ABS defines it as identifying \"different parent-child relationships within families\", coded from the relationship in household question with surnames and other form detail used to settle step against natural status when both parents are present. Unlike almost every other Census column it is not answered by the household: it comes from the ABS Address Register and is confirmed by field officers during collection. It sits beside AGEP, which is the ABS-derived age in completed years at Census night, and IFAGEP, which flags where age was imputed. The column is present in the 2011 and 2016 person tables only.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Age (AGEP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/age-agep","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Month of birth","k":"Calendar month of birth (1 to 12)","def":"A month number from 1 to 12, held as a component of a date rather than as a classification with meaning of its own.","p":"2011, 2016","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Age (AGEP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/age-agep","lim":"It is not a date of birth. No day of the month is carried, so an exact age cannot be computed and two people born in the same month cannot be ordered, which matters for any eligibility rule with a birthday cutoff. Where age was imputed rather than reported, the birth month cannot be a value the person supplied; ABS puts the age non-response rate at 5.6% in 2016, and IFAGEP on the same row marks those records.","where":["madip-ge-030101d-census2016-census2016person-2016 / census_2016_person","madipge-cen11-d-person-2011 / census_2011_person"]},{"n":"DOBYP","d":"The year in which the person was born, as reported on the 2011 or 2016 Census form.","full":"The year in which the person was born, as reported on the 2011 or 2016 Census form. It is the year component of the date of birth the Census collects to derive age: ABS states that \"Age is calculated from date of birth when provided, otherwise stated age is used\", and that where both a date of birth and a stated age are given, the date of birth wins unless it is identified as wrong. With DOBMP on the same row it gives a birth month and year that can be used for linking or for age at a reference date other than Census night. The column is present in the 2011 and 2016 person tables only.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Age (AGEP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/age-agep","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Year of birth","k":"Four-digit year of birth","def":"A four-digit calendar year. The range is open at the older end and bounded by the Census year at the younger end.","p":"2011, 2016","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Age (AGEP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/age-agep","lim":"Subtracting this year from the Census year does not give the person's age. A person born in December 2000 was 15 on 2016 Census night, 9 August, not 16, so AGEP is the ABS measure of age and this column will disagree with it for roughly the second half of each birth year. It also carries no day of the month, so it cannot serve as a complete date of birth for exact-match linking.","where":["madip-ge-030101d-census2016-census2016person-2016 / census_2016_person","madipge-cen11-d-person-2011 / census_2011_person"]},{"n":"DOMP","d":"How much unpaid housework the person did in the week before Census night, reported in bands.","full":"How much unpaid housework the person did in the week before Census night, reported in bands. It is one of three unpaid work columns on the person row: CHCAREP covers unpaid child care and UNCAREP covers unpaid care for a person with a disability or an older person, and a person can report all three. The column appears in the 2011, 2016 and 2021 person tables and applies to persons aged 15 and over.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Unpaid domestic work: number of hours (DOMP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/unpaid-work-and-care/unpaid-domestic-work-number-hours-domp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Unpaid Domestic Work: Number of Hours","t":"categorical","k":"Banded hours of unpaid domestic work in the previous week","def":"A single character: 1 nil hours, 2 less than 5 hours, 3 five to 14 hours, 4 fifteen to 29 hours, 5 thirty hours or more, & not stated, @ not applicable, V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Unpaid domestic work: number of hours (DOMP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/unpaid-work-and-care/unpaid-domestic-work-number-hours-domp","lim":"The bands are wide and open at the top, so a person doing 30 hours and a person doing 70 hours are the same value and no mean can be computed without assuming a midpoint. The reference week is the week before Census night, so illness, holidays or shift patterns in that one week carry straight into the answer; ABS reports a 6.6% non-response rate in 2021, down from 8.8% in 2016.","where":["madip-ge-030101d-census2016-census2016person-2016 / census_2016_person","madipge-cen11-d-person-2011 / census_2011_person","madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"],"dom":51},{"n":"DWELLING_ID","d":"The dwelling a Census record belongs to, used to attach a person or a family to the household they were counted in.","full":"The dwelling a Census record belongs to, used to attach a person or a family to the household they were counted in. In the 2021 tables it appears on the person, family and dwelling rows, so it is the key that carries tenure, dwelling structure and household income onto a person; in 2011 and 2016 it appears on the dwelling row only. ABS builds its Census microdata the same way, releasing dwelling, family and person records with identifiers \"available across levels: ABSFID and the related ABSHID on each family record; ABSPID and the related ABSFID and ABSHID on each person record\". In fplida the values are synthetic and are minted separately for each Census year.","dsrc":"ABS, Microdata and TableBuilder: Census of Population and Housing","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/microdata-tablebuilder/available-microdata-tablebuilder/census-population-and-housing","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Dwelling ID","k":"Census dwelling record identifier","def":"An arbitrary record key. A dwelling enumerated in 2016 and again in 2021 carries two unrelated identifiers, so the column cannot follow an address or a household over time; the Address Register identifier ARID, carried on the PLIDA Core address tables with start and end dates, is the key that does that. ABS defines the variable as classifying dwellings into \"Private dwellings (occupied and unoccupied), Non-private dwellings, Migratory, off-shore and shipping areas\". It is sourced from the ABS Address Register or set by field staff during enumeration, and it is the column that decides which other dwelling variables apply: income, tenure and family columns are coded @ for anything that is not an occupied private dwelling. The column appears in the 2011, 2016 and 2021 dwelling tables.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Dwelling type (DWTD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/dwelling-type-dwtd","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Dwelling Type","t":"categorical","k":"Census dwelling type classification","def":"A single digit: 1 occupied private dwelling, 2 unoccupied private dwelling, 3 non-private dwelling, 4 migratory, 5 off-shore, 6 shipping.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Dwelling type (DWTD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/dwelling-type-dwtd","lim":"Code 3 does not say what kind of non-private dwelling it is; NPDD carries hotel, hospital, prison, aged care and the rest. \"Unoccupied\" is partly a modelled outcome rather than an observation, because where contact could not be made ABS settles occupancy with the Census Occupancy Model, and ABS reports that a small number of people were wrongly coded to migratory, off-shore or shipping in 2021.","where":["madip-ge-030103d-census2016-census2016dwelling-2016 / census_2016_dwelling","madipge-cen11-d-dwelling-2011 / census_2011_dwelling","madipge-cen21-d-dwelling-2021 / census_2021_dwelling"],"dom":52},{"n":"EETP","d":"Whether the person was working, studying, doing both or doing neither, on a four-level engagement scale.","full":"Whether the person was working, studying, doing both or doing neither, on a four-level engagement scale. ABS defines it as indicating \"whether a person is engaged or not engaged in work and/or study\", and derives it by crossing three columns that also sit on the person row: labour force status and hours worked not stated (LFHRP), full-time or part-time student status (STUP) and age (AGEP). Full engagement means full-time work, full-time study, or a part-time combination of both; partial engagement means only one of the two, part-time. The column appears in the 2016 and 2021 person tables and applies to persons aged 15 and over.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Engagement in employment, education and training (EETP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/engagement-employment-education-and-training-eetp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Engagement in Employment Education and Training","t":"categorical","k":"Census engagement in employment, education and training classification","def":"A hierarchical code with seven one-digit values and twelve two-digit values beneath them: 1 fully engaged (11 to 15), 2 partially engaged (21 to 22), 3 at least partially engaged (31), 4 not engaged (41), plus & not stated and @ not applicable.","p":"2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Engagement in employment, education and training (EETP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/engagement-employment-education-and-training-eetp","lim":"Code 3, at least partially engaged, is a residual for records with too little information rather than a middle rung on the scale, so treating the codes as ordered puts unclassifiable people between the partially and the not engaged. Study means enrolment at an educational institution, so a person doing unaccredited training, unpaid care or job search only is coded not engaged.","where":["madip-ge-030101d-census2016-census2016person-2016 / census_2016_person","madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"],"dom":53},{"n":"EMFP","d":"A two-way split of the person into employed against everyone else, built for national reporting.","full":"A two-way split of the person into employed against everyone else, built for national reporting. ABS defines it as flagging \"whether a person is employed or unemployed/not in the labour force\", collapsing the full-time, part-time and away-from-work categories of labour force status (LFSP) into code 1 and the rest into code 2. It sits in the national reporting group of 2021 Census variables alongside UEFP, the unemployment flag, and LFFP, the labour force participation flag. It appears in the 2021 person table only and applies to persons aged 15 and over.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Employment flag (EMFP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/national-reporting-indicators/employment-flag-emfp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Employment flag","t":"categorical","k":"Binary employment flag for national reporting","def":"A single character: 1 employed, 2 unemployed or not in the labour force, @ not applicable, V overseas visitor.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Employment flag (EMFP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/national-reporting-indicators/employment-flag-emfp","lim":"Code 2 merges unemployed people with people outside the labour force, so no unemployment rate can be built from this column alone; UEFP and LFSP make that distinction. The values are of the right shape but are not a confirmed mapping.","where":["madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"],"dom":55},{"n":"EMPP","d":"How many people the person's own business employs, asked only of owner managers.","full":"How many people the person's own business employs, asked only of owner managers. ABS defines it as recording \"the number of employees (in ranges) employed by owner managers (excluding the owner managers themselves)\", so the respondent is not counted in their own figure. It applies to persons aged 15 and over who are owner managers of an incorporated or unincorporated enterprise, which makes status in employment (SIEMP in 2016 and 2021, EMTP in 2011) the column that decides who is in scope. The column appears in the 2011, 2016 and 2021 person tables.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Number of employees (EMPP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/number-employees-empp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Number of Employees","t":"categorical","k":"Banded count of employees of an owner manager's business","def":"A single character: 1 nil employees, 2 one to 19 employees, 3 twenty or more employees, & not stated, @ not applicable, V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Number of employees (EMPP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/number-employees-empp","lim":"It is not the size of the person's workplace. The 0.4% non-response rate in 2021 is low precisely because the column applies to so few people, not because the measure is precise.","where":["madip-ge-030101d-census2016-census2016person-2016 / census_2016_person","madipge-cen11-d-person-2011 / census_2011_person","madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"],"dom":56},{"n":"EMTP","d":"Whether the person worked as an employee, ran their own business, or worked unpaid in a family business, in the 2011 Census.","full":"Whether the person worked as an employee, ran their own business, or worked unpaid in a family business, in the 2011 Census. ABS defines the variable as classifying \"all employed people to either employees, owner-managers of incorporated enterprises, owner-managers of unincorporated enterprises, or contributing family workers, on the basis of their main job\". It applies only to people whose labour force status is employed, and it sits with GNGP, which splits employees between the public and private sectors, and EMPP, which counts an owner manager's employees. Boundaries are also redrawn each ASGS edition, so the 2021 codes on Edition 3 are not directly comparable with earlier Census geography.","where":["madipge-cen21-d-dwelling-2021 / census_2021_dwelling"]},{"n":"GCCSAP","d":"The greater capital city region, or the rest-of-state balance, of the person's usual residence at the 2021 Census.","full":"The greater capital city region, or the rest-of-state balance, of the person's usual residence at the 2021 Census. The \"(ur)\" in the custodian's label marks place of usual residence, which the ABS Census geography glossary describes as \"where a person usually lives\", as against place of enumeration, \"where a person was on Census night\". ABS defines the regions themselves as \"Geographic areas built from Statistical Areas Level 4 (SA4s)\" whose \"boundaries represent labour markets and the functional area of Australian capital cities\". It is the top of the person's usual residence geography hierarchy, above SA4UCP, SA3UCP, SA2UCP, SA1UCP and MBUCP, and is distinct from POWGCCSA, which is the region of the person's workplace.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Greater Capital City Statistical Areas","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/greater-capital-city-statistical-areas","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Greater capital city statistical areas (ur)","k":"ASGS Greater Capital City Statistical Area code","def":"A five-character alphanumeric ASGS code: a one-digit state or territory identifier then a four-character GCCSA identifier, for example 1GSYD for Greater Sydney. Edition 3 has 16 spatial GCCSAs plus 19 non-spatial special purpose codes.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Greater Capital City Statistical Areas","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/greater-capital-city-statistical-areas","lim":"It is not where the person was on Census night. Someone enumerated in a hotel in Greater Brisbane while usually living in Rest of NSW carries the Rest of NSW code here while the dwelling row they attach to carries Greater Brisbane in GCCSAD, so the two columns will disagree by design. People with no usual address are given a special purpose code rather than being left missing, so those records are present in the column but not locatable on a map.","where":["madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"]},{"n":"GNGP","d":"Whether the person's employer is a government body and at what level of government, or a private business.","full":"Whether the person's employer is a government body and at what level of government, or a private business. ABS defines the variable as classifying \"employed people according to whether they are employed in the government (public) or non-government (private) sector\", coded from the written employer business name and workplace address that the respondent supplies. It applies to employed persons aged 15 and over and describes the main job, sitting beside INDP for the employer's industry and OCCP for the person's own occupation. The column appears in the 2011, 2016 and 2021 person tables.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Public/private sector (GNGP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/publicprivate-sector-gngp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Public/Private Sector","t":"categorical","k":"Census public or private sector of employer","def":"A single character: 1 national government, 2 state or territory government, 3 local government, 4 private sector, & not stated, @ not applicable, V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Public/private sector (GNGP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/publicprivate-sector-gngp","lim":"Private sector is a default rather than a positive finding: ABS assigns anyone it cannot classify as public sector to code 4, so that category absorbs the doubtful cases and is overstated at the margin. Within the public sector, records that could not be split by level of government were imputed proportionally across national, state and local, so the three-way split is partly modelled and unreliable for small areas.","where":["madip-ge-030101d-census2016-census2016person-2016 / census_2016_person","madipge-cen11-d-person-2011 / census_2011_person","madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"],"dom":70},{"n":"HARTP","d":"Whether the person ticked arthritis on the 2021 Census long-term health conditions question.","full":"Whether the person ticked arthritis on the 2021 Census long-term health conditions question.
