It applies to all persons, including children.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has arthritis (HARTP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/health/whether-has-arthritis-hartp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Whether has arthritis","t":"categorical","k":"Census long-term health condition flag (arthritis)","def":"A three-character code: 011 has arthritis, 012 does not have arthritis, &&& not stated, VVV overseas visitor.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has arthritis (HARTP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/health/whether-has-arthritis-hartp","lim":"It does not separate osteoarthritis from rheumatoid arthritis, which are different diseases with different causes and treatments, and it carries no severity, treatment or date of onset. It is built during processing from family composition (FMCF) and household composition (HHCD), so it carries both facts in one code. This variable does not indicate whether a person has multiple long-term health conditions.\" It is one of ten separate condition flags added to the person record for the first time in 2021, all struck from the same tick-box question, so HLTHP beside it answers whether any condition was reported and HOLHP catches conditions outside the ten.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has diabetes (excluding gestational diabetes) (HDIAP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/health/whether-has-diabetes-excluding-gestational-diabetes-hdiap","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Whether has diabetes (excluding gestational diabetes)","t":"categorical","k":"Census long-term health condition flag (diabetes)","def":"Two substantive codes, 051 has diabetes and 052 does not, with &&& for not stated and VVV for an overseas visitor.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has diabetes (excluding gestational diabetes) (HDIAP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/health/whether-has-diabetes-excluding-gestational-diabetes-hdiap","lim":"It records a reported diagnosis, not a clinical record, and the Census does not separate type 1 from type 2 diabetes, so the two cannot be counted apart. It is one of the ten condition flags new to the 2021 person record; because each condition has its own column, combinations have to be built by crossing them, and ABS publishes ready-made pair variables such as CODBHDP for diabetes and heart disease.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has heart disease (including heart attack or angina) (HHEDP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/health/whether-has-heart-disease-including-heart-attack-or-angina-hhedp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Whether has heart disease (including heart attack or angina)","t":"categorical","k":"Census long-term health condition flag (heart disease)","def":"Codes 061 has heart disease and 062 does not, with &&& not stated and VVV overseas visitor.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has heart disease (including heart attack or angina) (HHEDP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/health/whether-has-heart-disease-including-heart-attack-or-angina-hhedp","lim":"A tick covers everything from a past heart attack to managed angina, so it carries no severity, no date of onset and no current treatment status. ABS defines it as identifying \"households where people were absent from the dwelling on Census Night, did not state their income, or stated a negative income\". It sits on the dwelling record for 2011, 2016 and 2021 and is the household income column to use for living-standard comparisons, where HIND is the unadjusted total.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Equivalised total household income (weekly) (HIED)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/equivalised-total-household-income-weekly-hied","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Equivalised Total Household Income (weekly)","t":"categorical","k":"Equivalised weekly household income range","def":"Nineteen categories: sixteen income ranges from nil income up to $3,500 or more a week ($182,000 a year), plus code 17 partial income stated, && all incomes not stated and @@ not applicable. It is the permissive twin of HIND, which sends the same households to a partial-income code instead, and HIDD on the same row says which households the two columns treat differently.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Total household income as stated (weekly) (HINASD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/total-household-income-stated-weekly-hinasd","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Total Household Income as Stated (weekly)","t":"categorical","k":"Weekly household income range as stated","def":"Twenty-two income brackets from negative income up to $8,000 or more a week ($416,000 a year), plus && all incomes not stated and @@ not applicable. Personal incomes are reported in ranges, so median values from the Survey of Income and Housing are assigned to each band before summing.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Total household income as stated (weekly) (HINASD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/total-household-income-stated-weekly-hinasd","lim":"A stated total from an incomplete household understates that household's real income, and nothing in this column says by how much or how many members were missing. HINASD on the same row is the version that still adds up what was stated, so comparing the two shows how much of the income distribution rests on incomplete households.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Total household income (weekly) (HIND)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/total-household-income-weekly-hind","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Total Household Income (weekly)","t":"categorical","k":"Weekly household income range","def":"Twenty-five categories, from negative income and nil income through weekly ranges up to $8,000 or more ($416,000 a year), with separate codes for partial income stated, all incomes not stated and not applicable. This variable does not indicate whether a person has multiple long-term health conditions.\" It is one of the ten condition flags added to the 2021 person record, and in PLIDA it can be checked against dialysis and transplant activity in the MBS and PBS products for the same person.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has kidney disease (HKIDP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/health/whether-has-kidney-disease-hkidp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Whether has kidney disease","t":"categorical","k":"Census long-term health condition flag (kidney disease)","def":"Codes 071 has kidney disease and 072 does not, with &&& not stated and VVV overseas visitor.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has kidney disease (HKIDP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/health/whether-has-kidney-disease-hkidp","lim":"It gives no stage, no function measure and no treatment status, so early chronic kidney disease and end-stage disease on dialysis are the same tick. It is the Census-side counterpart to mental-health item use in the PBS and MBS products for the same person, and is the only mental health measure on the Census person record.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has mental health condition (including depression or anxiety) (HMHCP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/health/whether-has-mental-health-condition-including-depression-or-anxiety-hmhcp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Whether has mental health condition (including depression or anxiety)","t":"categorical","k":"Census long-term health condition flag (mental health condition)","def":"Codes 091 has a mental health condition and 092 does not, with &&& not stated and VVV overseas visitor.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Whether has mental health condition (including depression or anxiety) (HMHCP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/health/whether-has-mental-health-condition-including-depression-or-anxiety-hmhcp","lim":"It cannot separate depression from anxiety from any other diagnosis, and it requires a person to have been told by a clinician, so undiagnosed and untreated conditions are absent by construction. ABS defines it as \"a measure of housing utilisation based on a comparison of the number of bedrooms in a dwelling with a series of household demographics\", applying the Canadian National Occupancy Standard: no more than two people to a bedroom, children under 5 of different sexes may share, children under 18 of the same sex may share, and single adults and couples each need their own room. It sits on the dwelling record for 2016 and 2021 and is the ABS measure behind overcrowding counts, since needing one or more extra bedrooms is the usual overcrowding threshold.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Housing suitability (HOSD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/housing-suitability-hosd","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Housing Suitability","k":"Canadian National Occupancy Standard bedroom surplus or shortfall","def":"Nine ordered categories from 01 four or more extra bedrooms needed through 05 no bedrooms needed or spare to 09 four or more bedrooms spare, plus 10 unable to determine, && not stated and @@ not applicable, twelve categories in all.","p":"2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Housing suitability (HOSD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/housing-suitability-hosd","lim":"It is a rule applied to bedroom counts and household demographics, not a judgement about the dwelling. ABS defines Indigenous Areas as \"medium sized geographic areas built from whole Indigenous Locations. They are designed for the release and analysis of more detailed statistics for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people.\" It is the middle rung of the three Indigenous geographies on the dwelling record, above ILOCD and below IREGD, and the enumeration counterpart of IAREP, which places a person by usual residence.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Indigenous Areas","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/indigenous-structure/indigenous-areas","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Indigenous area (en)","k":"ASGS Indigenous Area code","def":"A six-digit hierarchical ASGS code: one digit for state or territory, two for the Indigenous Region and three for the Indigenous Area. They are designed for the release and analysis of more detailed statistics for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people.\" It is the usual-residence counterpart of IARED on the dwelling record, and it sits between ILOCP and IREGP as the middle rung of the Indigenous geography hierarchy on the person table.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Indigenous Areas","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/indigenous-structure/indigenous-areas","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Indigenous area (ur)","k":"ASGS Indigenous Area code","def":"A six-digit hierarchical ASGS code: one digit for state or territory, two for the Indigenous Region and three for the Indigenous Area. Nor does it identify who the donor record was, so imputed statuses cannot be checked or re-derived.","where":["madip-ge-030101d-census2016-census2016person-2016 / census_2016_person","madipge-cen11-d-person-2011 / census_2011_person","madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"],"dom":94},{"n":"IFNMFD","d":"Whether the people counted in this occupied private dwelling came from a returned form or were created by the ABS because no form came back.","full":"Whether the people counted in this occupied private dwelling came from a returned form or were created by the ABS because no form came back. The dictionary defines it as indicating \"whether the number of males and females were counted for an occupied private dwelling or were imputed\". It is the strongest data-quality flag on the dwelling record for 2011, 2016 and 2021, because where it says imputed, only sex, age, registered marital status and place of usual residence carry imputed values and every other person variable in the dwelling reads not stated or not applicable.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Imputation flag for number of males and females in dwelling (IFNMFD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/imputation-flag-number-males-and-females-dwelling-ifnmfd","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Imputation Flag for Number of Males and Females in Dwelling","t":"categorical","k":"Census imputation flag (persons imputed into dwelling)","def":"Three codes: 1 persons not imputed into dwelling, 2 persons imputed into dwelling and @ not applicable, the last covering unoccupied dwellings, non-private dwellings and migratory, off-shore and shipping SA1s.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Imputation flag for number of males and females in dwelling (IFNMFD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/household-and-families/imputation-flag-number-males-and-females-dwelling-ifnmfd","lim":"An imputed dwelling is not a partly missing dwelling, it is a wholly constructed one, so counting its residents in any analysis of income, employment, education or health silently adds people whose only real attributes are sex, age, marital status and residence. The flag also gives no rate of its own, since it reflects processing method rather than item non-response.","where":["madip-ge-030103d-census2016-census2016dwelling-2016 / census_2016_dwelling","madipge-cen11-d-dwelling-2011 / census_2011_dwelling","madipge-cen21-d-dwelling-2021 / census_2021_dwelling"],"dom":95},{"n":"IFPOWP","d":"Whether the workplace address on this record was coded from what the person wrote or imputed, and how coarse the stated part was.","full":"Whether the workplace address on this record was coded from what the person wrote or imputed, and how coarse the stated part was. The dictionary defines it as indicating \"if a person's place of work in the week before Census Night was imputed, and to what geographic level\". On the PLIDA person record for 2016 and 2021 it is the quality flag for the workplace geography columns beside it, IMPSA2WKADP and IMPSTEWKADP in 2016, so a code of 4 means only the state was stated and everything finer was filled in.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Imputation flag for place of work (IFPOWP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/imputation-flag-place-work-ifpowp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Imputation Flag for Place of Work","t":"categorical","k":"Census imputation flag (place of work, by geographic level)","def":"Five substantive codes, 1 workplace address not imputed, 2 imputed with SA2 stated, 3 imputed with capital city stated, 4 imputed with state or territory stated and 5 imputed with nothing stated, plus @ not applicable and V overseas visitor.","p":"2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Imputation flag for place of work (IFPOWP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/imputation-flag-place-work-ifpowp","lim":"It is not a measure of accuracy for the workplace address itself. In 2021 the bigger problem was people entering their home address while working from home during lockdown, and an address like that is not imputed, so this flag reads 1 for it. ABS puts the place of work non-response rate at 11.1% in 2021, up from 10.0% in 2016.","where":["madip-ge-030101d-census2016-census2016person-2016 / census_2016_person","madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"],"dom":96},{"n":"IFPURP","d":"Whether the person's usual address was coded from what they wrote or imputed, and at which level of the geographic hierarchy the imputation started.","full":"Whether the person's usual address was coded from what they wrote or imputed, and at which level of the geographic hierarchy the imputation started. The dictionary defines it as indicating \"if a person's place of usual residence was imputed in the Census, and to what geographic level\". It is on the person record for 2011, 2016 and 2021 and it is the quality flag for every usual-residence geography column on the same row, so an SA1 of usual residence with a flag of 3 or 4 was chosen for the person rather than reported by them.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Imputation flag for place of usual residence (IFPURP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/imputation-flag-place-usual-residence-ifpurp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Imputation Flag for Place of Usual Residence","t":"categorical","k":"Census imputation flag (place of usual residence, by geographic level)","def":"Four codes: 01 not imputed with state or territory, SA2 and SA1 all stated; 02 SA1 imputed; 03 SA2 and SA1 imputed with state or territory or capital city given; and 04 state or territory, SA2 and SA1 all imputed.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Imputation flag for place of usual residence (IFPURP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/imputation-flag-place-usual-residence-ifpurp","lim":"An unimputed flag does not mean the address is right, only that a codeable one was supplied; a stale or mistaken address passes as code 01. ABS puts the SA2-level non-response at 4.3% in 2021, down from 5.4% in 2016.","where":["madip-ge-030101d-census2016-census2016person-2016 / census_2016_person","madipge-cen11-d-person-2011 / census_2011_person","madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"],"dom":97},{"n":"IFSEXP","d":"Whether the person's sex on this record was reported or filled in by the ABS.","full":"Whether the person's sex on this record was reported or filled in by the ABS. The dictionary defines it as indicating \"if a person's binary sex was imputed. Imputation is a statistical process for predicting values where no response was provided to a question and a response could not be derived.\" It is on the person record for 2016 and 2021 and is created during processing of SEXP beside it; ABS reports 4.7% of sex values were imputed in 2021, down from 5.8% in 2016.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Imputation flag for sex (IFSEXP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/imputation-flag-sex-ifsexp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Imputation Flag for Sex","t":"categorical","k":"Census imputation flag (sex)","def":"Two codes: 01 sex not imputed and 02 sex imputed.","p":"2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Imputation flag for sex (IFSEXP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/imputation-flag-sex-ifsexp","lim":"The flag is about binary sex only. It has nothing to say about the separate 2021 non-binary sex response, and a record flagged as not imputed can still be a form filled in by another household member rather than the person concerned.","where":["madip-ge-030101d-census2016-census2016person-2016 / census_2016_person","madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"],"dom":98},{"n":"ILOCD","d":"The Indigenous Location the dwelling was in when it was enumerated on Census night 2021, the finest of the three Indigenous geographies on the dwelling record.","full":"The Indigenous Location the dwelling was in when it was enumerated on Census night 2021, the finest of the three Indigenous geographies on the dwelling record. ABS builds them from whole SA1s to represent \"small Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities (urban and rural) that are near each other or that share language, traditional borders or Native Title\", with a minimum population of about 90 people. ILOCD nests inside IARED and IREGD on the same row, so the three columns are one address at three scales.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Indigenous Locations","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/indigenous-structure/indigenous-locations","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Indigenous location (en)","k":"ASGS Indigenous Location code","def":"An eight-digit hierarchical ASGS code: one digit for state or territory, two for the Indigenous Region, three for the Indigenous Area and two for the Indigenous Location, for example 40101303 Raukkan. There are 1,139 Indigenous Locations covering all of Australia, including 19 non-spatial special purpose codes.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Indigenous Locations","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/indigenous-structure/indigenous-locations","lim":"The small population that makes the geography useful also makes it disclosive, so a cross-tabulation at this level will often be perturbed or suppressed in cleared output. And because it records where the dwelling was counted, not where its residents live, a dwelling occupied by visitors on Census night carries a location that describes none of them.","where":["madipge-cen21-d-dwelling-2021 / census_2021_dwelling"]},{"n":"ILOCP","d":"The Indigenous Location of the person's usual residence at the 2021 Census, the finest Indigenous geography on the person record.","full":"The Indigenous Location of the person's usual residence at the 2021 Census, the finest Indigenous geography on the person record. ABS builds them from whole SA1s to represent \"small Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities (urban and rural) that are near each other or that share language, traditional borders or Native Title\", with a minimum population of about 90 people. It nests inside IAREP and IREGP on the same row, and IFPURP says whether the usual residence behind all three was imputed.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Indigenous Locations","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/indigenous-structure/indigenous-locations","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Indigenous location (ur)","k":"ASGS Indigenous Location code","def":"An eight-digit hierarchical ASGS code: one digit for state or territory, two for the Indigenous Region, three for the Indigenous Area and two for the Indigenous Location. The small populations behind these codes also mean cell counts at this level rarely survive disclosure control.","where":["madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"]},{"n":"IMPSA2WKADP","d":"The SA2 the person's workplace address fell in during the week before Census night 2016, after ABS imputation filled any gaps.","full":"The SA2 the person's workplace address fell in during the week before Census night 2016, after ABS imputation filled any gaps. ABS describes place of work as recording \"the geographic area in which a person worked in the week before Census Night\", with the workplace address coded to a Destination Zone and then aggregated to SA2, SA3, SA4, greater capital city and state. In PLIDA's 2016 person table this SA2 is the finest workplace geography supplied, since the Destination Zone itself is not carried, and IFPOWP beside it says whether the value was reported or imputed.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of work (POWP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-work-powp","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Imputed SA2 of workplace address","k":"ASGS Statistical Area Level 2 code (workplace)","def":"A nine-digit ASGS Statistical Area Level 2 code, the standard workplace geography output of place of work coding.","p":"2016","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of work (POWP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-work-powp","lim":"It is the workplace, not the employer, and not the person's home. Comparing it with the usual-residence SA2 on the same row gives a commuting pair, but neither an employer identity nor a distance travelled, and where IFPOWP shows imputation the SA2 was assigned rather than reported.","where":["madip-ge-030101d-census2016-census2016person-2016 / census_2016_person"]},{"n":"IMPSTEWKADP","d":"The state or territory the person's workplace address fell in during the week before Census night 2016, after ABS imputation filled any gaps.","full":"The state or territory the person's workplace address fell in during the week before Census night 2016, after ABS imputation filled any gaps. It is the coarsest rung of the same place of work coding that produced IMPSA2WKADP on the row, since ABS codes the workplace address to a Destination Zone and then up through SA2, SA3, SA4, greater capital city and state. Its value is that it survives when the finer workplace geography does not: IFPOWP code 4 means the state was stated and everything below it was imputed.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of work (POWP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-work-powp","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Imputed state/territory of workplace address","k":"ASGS State and Territory code (workplace)","def":"A one-digit ASGS state and territory code, 1 New South Wales through 8 Australian Capital Territory, with codes 9 and above for other territories and special purpose areas.","p":"2016","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of work (POWP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-work-powp","lim":"A state of workplace cannot show interstate commuting patterns at any useful resolution, and it hides the very large share of Australian employment concentrated in a handful of capital city SA2s. Where the finer geography was imputed rather than stated, IMPSA2WKADP is not an independent check on this column, because both come from the same address.","where":["madip-ge-030101d-census2016-census2016person-2016 / census_2016_person"]},{"n":"INCP","d":"The band the person put themselves in when asked what they usually receive each week, from all sources before tax.","full":"The band the person put themselves in when asked what they usually receive each week, from all sources before tax. ABS defines it as indicating \"the total income (in ranges) that a person usually receives each week\". It is on the person record for 2011, 2016 and 2021, and it is the input the ABS sums to build HIND, HINASD and HIED on the dwelling record, using Survey of Income and Housing medians in place of each band. In PLIDA it is the self-reported income to set against the ATO's assessed income in the PIT products for the same person.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Total personal income (weekly) (INCP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/total-personal-income-weekly-incp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Total Personal Income (weekly)","t":"categorical","k":"Weekly total personal income range","def":"Sixteen bands from negative income and nil income through $1 to $149 a week up to $3,500 or more a week ($182,000 a year), with && not stated, @@ not applicable for people under 15 and VV overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Total personal income (weekly) (INCP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/total-personal-income-weekly-incp","lim":"It is usual income as the respondent understands it, not a measured amount for any period, so it does not reconcile with taxable income on a tax return and cannot be used to test tax compliance. The top band is open, so no mean income can be computed from it, and non-response was 7.2% in 2021.","where":["madip-ge-030101d-census2016-census2016person-2016 / census_2016_person","madipge-cen11-d-person-2011 / census_2011_person","madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"],"dom":99},{"n":"INDP","d":"The industry of the person's main job in the week before Census night, coded to ANZSIC.","full":"The industry of the person's main job in the week before Census night, coded to ANZSIC. ABS defines it as describing \"the industry of the main job held by the employed person in the week prior to Census night\", built by matching the business name and address written on the form against ABS lists of businesses whose main industry activity is already known, and coding the industry and goods or services descriptions by hand where no match is found. It is on the person record for 2011, 2016 and 2021, and it is the Census-side industry to compare with the ANZSIC on the employer's BLADE record for the same period.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Industry of employment (INDP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/industry-employment-indp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Industry of Employment","t":"categorical","k":"ANZSIC industry of employment code","def":"Codes from the Australian and New Zealand Standard Industrial Classification 2006 (Revision 2.0): 20 categories at one digit, 106 at two, 293 at three and 721 at four, with &&&& not stated, @@@@ not applicable and VVVV overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Industry of employment (INDP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/industry-employment-indp","lim":"It is the main job only, so a second job in another industry is invisible, and it is the industry of the employing business rather than the work the person does, which is OCCP. A cleaner in a hospital and a surgeon both code to Health Care and Social Assistance.","where":["madip-ge-030101d-census2016-census2016person-2016 / census_2016_person","madipge-cen11-d-person-2011 / census_2011_person","madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"],"dom":100},{"n":"INGDWTD","d":"Whether at least one person counted at home in this dwelling identified as Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander.","full":"Whether at least one person counted at home in this dwelling identified as Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander. ABS defines it as indicating \"households which have at least one person who identified as being Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander\", derived from the usual address indicator, Indigenous status and household composition. It is on the dwelling record for 2011, 2016 and 2021, and it is what makes a household-level Indigenous analysis possible, since INGP is a person attribute and INGF does the same job for a family.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Indigenous household indicator (INGDWTD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/indigenous-household-indicator-ingdwtd","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Indigenous Household Indicator","t":"categorical","k":"Indigenous household indicator","def":"Three codes: 1 household with Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander person(s), 2 other households and @ not applicable for non-private and unoccupied dwellings.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Indigenous household indicator (INGDWTD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/indigenous-household-indicator-ingdwtd","lim":"People who were temporarily absent on Census night are excluded from the derivation, so a household whose only Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander member was away reads as an other household. The 2021 Post Enumeration Survey also put the net undercount of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people at 170,752, a rate of 17.4%, so the flag understates such households more than a general undercount would.","where":["madip-ge-030103d-census2016-census2016dwelling-2016 / census_2016_dwelling","madipge-cen11-d-dwelling-2011 / census_2011_dwelling","madipge-cen21-d-dwelling-2021 / census_2021_dwelling"],"dom":101},{"n":"INGF","d":"Whether at least one member of this family identified as Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander and was at home on Census night 2021.","full":"Whether at least one member of this family identified as Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander and was at home on Census night 2021. ABS defines the flagged group as \"Families with at least one person who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander origin, who is a usual resident in the dwelling, and was at home on Census Night.\" It sits on the family record, where INGDWTD does the same job for the dwelling and INGP for the person, and it is derived from the usual address indicator, Indigenous status and family composition.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander family indicator (INGF)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-family-indicator-ingf","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Aboriginal and torres strait islander family indicator","t":"categorical","k":"Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander family indicator","def":"Four codes: 1 family with Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander person(s), 2 other families, & not stated and @ not applicable for non-family and non-classifiable households, unoccupied and non-private dwellings and migratory, off-shore and shipping SA1s.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander family indicator (INGF)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-family-indicator-ingf","lim":"The test requires usual residence and presence on the night at once, so a family whose Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander member was visiting elsewhere is coded as an other family. A dwelling can also hold several families, and the flag is set family by family, so INGDWTD on the dwelling can read yes while a particular family in it reads no.","where":["madipge-cen21-d-family-2021 / census_2021_family"],"dom":102},{"n":"INGP","d":"Whether the person identified as being of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander origin on the Census form.","full":"Whether the person identified as being of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander origin on the Census form. ABS defines it as recording \"the response of persons who identified themselves as being of Australian Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander origin in the Census\". It is on the person record for 2011, 2016 and 2021, and it is the input to INGDWTD on the dwelling record and INGF on the family record; in PLIDA it is also the Census answer to compare with the Indigenous status recorded administratively in DOMINO, MBS and the health datasets.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Indigenous status (INGP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/indigenous-status-ingp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Indigenous Status","t":"categorical","k":"Census Indigenous status classification","def":"Four substantive codes: 1 non-Indigenous, 2 Aboriginal, 3 Torres Strait Islander and 4 both Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander, with & not stated and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Indigenous status (INGP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/indigenous-status-ingp","lim":"It is self-identification at one moment, and it is never imputed: where the answer is unclear the record is coded not stated rather than filled in, so 4.9% of 2021 records carry no status at all. Change in the counts between censuses reflects people choosing to identify differently as much as any change in the population, and the 2021 Post Enumeration Survey put the net undercount at 170,752 people, a rate of 17.4%.","where":["madip-ge-030101d-census2016-census2016person-2016 / census_2016_person","madipge-cen11-d-person-2011 / census_2011_person","madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"],"dom":103},{"n":"IREGD","d":"The Indigenous Region the dwelling was in when it was enumerated on Census night 2021, the broadest of the three Indigenous geographies on the dwelling record.","full":"The Indigenous Region the dwelling was in when it was enumerated on Census night 2021, the broadest of the three Indigenous geographies on the dwelling record. ABS defines them as \"large geographic areas built from whole Indigenous Areas and are based on historical boundaries.\" With only 59 regions covering Australia, it is the level at which Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander analysis usually survives disclosure control, where ILOCD and IARED on the same row often will not.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Indigenous Regions","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/indigenous-structure/indigenous-regions","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Indigenous region (en)","k":"ASGS Indigenous Region code","def":"A three-digit hierarchical ASGS code, one digit for state or territory and two for the region, for example 304 Mount Isa. Being a dwelling enumeration geography, it also places visitors, not just residents.","where":["madipge-cen21-d-dwelling-2021 / census_2021_dwelling"]},{"n":"IREGP","d":"The Indigenous Region of the person's usual residence at the 2021 Census, the broadest Indigenous geography on the person record.","full":"The Indigenous Region of the person's usual residence at the 2021 Census, the broadest Indigenous geography on the person record. ABS defines them as \"large geographic areas built from whole Indigenous Areas and are based on historical boundaries.\" It is the level most Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander outputs are published at, because the 59 regions carry enough population for detailed cross-tabulation where IAREP and ILOCP on the same row do not.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Indigenous Regions","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/indigenous-structure/indigenous-regions","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Indigenous region (ur)","k":"ASGS Indigenous Region code","def":"A three-digit hierarchical ASGS code, one digit for state or territory and two for the region. There are 59 Indigenous Regions covering all of Australia, plus 19 non-spatial special purpose codes.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Indigenous Regions","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs-edition-3/jul2021-jun2026/indigenous-structure/indigenous-regions","lim":"Everybody usually resident in the region carries the code, so it counts population in a place rather than membership of a community, and INGP is the column that says who identified. The boundaries are also historical administrative lines, not nations or language groups.","where":["madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"]},{"n":"LANP","d":"The main language other than English the person uses at home, or English where no other language is used.","full":"The main language other than English the person uses at home, or English where no other language is used. The variable identifies whether a person uses a language other than English at home and records that language, classified to the Australian Standard Classification of Languages, 2016. It is on the person record for 2011, 2016 and 2021, and ENGLP beside it carries how well the person speaks English, which this column does not. Scope is dwellings owned with a mortgage or purchased under a shared equity scheme, so owner-occupiers without a loan and renters are not applicable.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Mortgage repayments (monthly) ranges (MRERD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/mortgage-repayments-monthly-ranges-mrerd","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Mortgage Repayments (monthly) Ranges","t":"categorical","k":"Monthly mortgage repayment range code","def":"A two-digit code from 01 to 21, running 01 nil repayments, 02 $1 to $149, then bands that widen with the amount: $150 wide to $599, $200 wide to $2,999, $500 wide to $3,999, 20 for $4,000 to $4,999 and 21 for $5,000 and over, with && not stated and @@ not applicable. The ABS explains that these regions \"are based on catchments or bioregions\", that \"the Australian government, in association with state and territory governments, has identified 56 regions covering all of Australia\", and that they exist \"to administer and report on aspects of environmental policy including sustainable farming and biodiversity\". The (en) suffix marks it as place of enumeration, so NRMRP is the matching column for a person's usual residence.","dsrc":"ABS, Census geography glossary, 2021 Census","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/geography/census-geography-glossary","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Natural resource management regions (en)","k":"Natural resource management region code, place of enumeration","def":"A code identifying one of the 56 natural resource management regions covering Australia, approximated by the ABS from mesh blocks so that Census counts can be reported on catchment and bioregion boundaries.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Census geography glossary, 2021 Census","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/geography/census-geography-glossary","lim":"These are not statistical regions and were dropped from the standard geography: the ABS states that \"Natural Resource Management Regions are no longer included in Non ABS Structures as they were found to be rarely used\", so no maintained correspondence exists between them and the SA and LGA structures. The ABS says these regions \"are based on catchments or bioregions\" and that 56 of them cover all of Australia, used \"to administer and report on aspects of environmental policy including sustainable farming and biodiversity\". Because it is coded on usual residence rather than Census-night location, it is the column to use when the question is about the resident population of a catchment, and NRMRD gives the enumeration-based equivalent on the dwelling table.","dsrc":"ABS, Census geography glossary, 2021 Census","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/geography/census-geography-glossary","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Natural resource management regions (ur)","k":"Natural resource management region code, place of usual residence","def":"A code identifying one of the 56 natural resource management regions covering Australia, allocated from the person's usual residence mesh block in MBUCP.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Census geography glossary, 2021 Census","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/geography/census-geography-glossary","lim":"The region tells you nothing about the person's relationship to the land or water it manages, so a city dweller inside a catchment carries the same code as a farmer on an irrigated property. OCCP on the same row holds the same job coded to ANZSCO 2013 Version 1.3, and OCSKEV1P holds the skill level implied by this column.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Occupation experimental update version 1 (OCCEV1P)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/occupation-experimental-update-version-1-occev1p","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Occupation experimental update version 1","t":"categorical","k":"ANZSCO 2021 Australian Update occupation code","def":"A six-digit hierarchical code from ANZSCO 2021 Australian Update, nesting one-digit major groups inside two-digit sub-major, three-digit minor and four-digit unit groups, with 'nfd' codes where a response supports only a broader level, plus supplementary codes for inadequately described, not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Occupation experimental update version 1 (OCCEV1P)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/occupation-experimental-update-version-1-occev1p","lim":"It is not comparable with OCCP beside it or with occupation in the 2011 and 2016 tables, because only part of the classification was rebuilt, so differences between the two columns are classification artefacts in the updated areas and nothing at all elsewhere. It is derived from the written occupation title and duties on the form, and INDP holds the industry of the same job while OCSKP holds its skill level.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Occupation (OCCP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/occupation-occp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Occupation","t":"categorical","k":"ANZSCO 2013 Version 1.3 occupation code","def":"A six-digit hierarchical ANZSCO code, with 8 major groups at one digit, 51 sub-major at two, 134 minor at three, 478 unit groups at four and 1,357 occupations at six. The ABS is explicit that \"the skill level is set by the person's occupation (OCCP), rather than the skill level of the person themselves\", and that this version \"has been created based on the ANZSCO - Australian and New Zealand Standard Classification of Occupations, 2021 Australian Update\". It is the companion of OCCEV1P in the way OCSKP is the companion of OCCP.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Occupation skill level experimental update version 1 (OCSKEV1P)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/income-and-work/occupation-skill-level-experimental-update-version-1-ocskev1p","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Occupation skill level experimental update version 1","t":"categorical","k":"ANZSCO skill level, 2021 Australian Update basis","def":"A single digit from 1 to 5, where 1 is the highest skill level and 5 the lowest, with 9 for skill level not determined, & not stated, @ not applicable and V overseas visitor. The ABS defines these as \"administrative health regions established to deliver primary care services for patients, as well as coordinate with local hospitals to improve the overall operational efficiency of the network\". The (en) suffix marks the coding basis as place of enumeration, and PHNP is the equivalent coded on usual residence. It is the natural join key for linking Census characteristics to MBS, PBS and hospital data reported by network.","dsrc":"ABS, Census geography glossary, 2021 Census","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/geography/census-geography-glossary","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Primary health networks (en)","k":"Primary health network region code, place of enumeration","def":"A code identifying one primary health network, approximated from mesh blocks. The ABS defines these regions as \"administrative health regions established to deliver primary care services for patients, as well as coordinate with local hospitals\", and the (ur) suffix means the code is allocated from usual residence rather than from where the person spent Census night. A postal area is not a postcode: the ABS builds it as \"an ABS Mesh Block approximation of a general definition of postcodes\" so that Census data can be lined up with records collected by postcode. It appears on the dwelling and family tables, with POAP giving the same approximation on a person's usual residence.","dsrc":"ABS, ASGS Edition 3, Non ABS Structures: Postal Areas","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/non-abs-structures/postal-areas","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Postal areas (en)","k":"ASGS postal area code, place of enumeration","def":"A four-digit code that matches a postcode number where one exists. ASGS Edition 3 defines 2,644 postal areas covering Australia without gaps or overlaps, including three non-spatial special purpose codes.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, ASGS Edition 3, Non ABS Structures: Postal Areas","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/non-abs-structures/postal-areas","lim":"Joining an external postcode-coded file to it will lose and misplace records. The ABS excludes post office box, mail-back and other non-street-delivery postcodes entirely, allocates each mesh block to a single postal area on population share where a mesh block spans two postcodes, and a handful of areas cross state borders, among them 0872, 2540, 2611, 2620, 2618, 2406 and 3707.","where":["madipge-cen21-d-dwelling-2021 / census_2021_dwelling","madipge-cen21-d-family-2021 / census_2021_family"]},{"n":"POAP","d":"The postal area covering the address where the person usually lives.","full":"The postal area covering the address where the person usually lives. It is an approximation rather than the postcode itself: the ABS builds it as \"an ABS Mesh Block approximation of a general definition of postcodes\" and warns that \"ABS approximations of administrative boundaries do not match official legal boundaries and should only be used for statistical purposes\". It is derived from MBUCP, the usual-residence mesh block, and is the practical bridge from Census characteristics to any administrative file that only records a postcode.","dsrc":"ABS, ASGS Edition 3, Non ABS Structures: Postal Areas","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/non-abs-structures/postal-areas","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Postal areas (ur)","k":"ASGS postal area code, place of usual residence","def":"A four-digit code matching a postcode number where one exists, drawn from the 2,644 postal areas in ASGS Edition 3, which include three non-spatial special purpose codes.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, ASGS Edition 3, Non ABS Structures: Postal Areas","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/non-abs-structures/postal-areas","lim":"Postal area boundaries are frozen for the life of an ASGS edition, so a postcode that Australia Post changes between 2021 and 2026 will not be reflected here and a join to recent administrative data will drift. The dictionary says \"the address of the person's workplace is coded to a Destination zone (DZN)\" and that destination zones \"are co-designed with state and territory transport authorities for the analysis of Place of work (POWP) data, commuting patterns and the development of transport policy\". POWSA2, POWSA3, POWSA4, POWLGA, POWGCCSA and POWSTE on the same row are aggregations of this code.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of work (POWP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-work-powp","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Destination zone (pow)","k":"ASGS destination zone code, place of work","def":"A nine-digit code made of a one-digit state or territory identifier, a four-digit SA2 identifier and a four-digit destination zone identifier, as in 111728922. The ABS says these areas \"are designed to represent the functional area of each of the eight State and Territory capital cities\" and that their boundaries \"represent labour markets\", which makes this the coarsest useful cut of commuting on the person record. Paired with GCCSAP, the usual residence version, it identifies people who work in a capital city but live outside it.","dsrc":"ABS, ASGS Edition 3, Main Structure: Greater Capital City Statistical Areas","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/greater-capital-city-statistical-areas","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Greater capital city statistical area (pow)","k":"ASGS greater capital city statistical area code, place of work","def":"A five-character alphanumeric code: one digit for the state or territory then a four-character area identifier, as in 1GSYD for Greater Sydney. It is one of the geographies the Census dictionary lists for place of work data, built by aggregating the destination zone in POWDZN, and the ABS describes local government areas as \"an ABS Mesh Block approximation of gazetted local government boundaries\". Set against LGAP, the council area of usual residence, it gives council-to-council commuting flows for 2021.","dsrc":"ABS, ASGS Edition 3, Non ABS Structures: Local Government Areas","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/non-abs-structures/local-government-areas","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Local government areas (2021 boundaries) (pow)","k":"ASGS local government area code (2021 boundaries), place of work","def":"A five-digit code, one digit for the state or territory and four for the area identifier, unique within the state and always ending in zero. Non-spatial codes include 9799 for migratory, offshore and shipping and 9499 for no usual address.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, ASGS Edition 3, Non ABS Structures: Local Government Areas","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/non-abs-structures/local-government-areas","lim":"The workplace is the address the person or their employer nominated, so people with no fixed workplace are coded to a depot and people directed to enter 'None' are coded to a non-spatial code rather than to a council, which biases commuting flows away from mobile trades and transport work. Use whichever vintage matches the council data being joined, and LGAP22 for the person's own council on the same vintage.","dsrc":"ABS, ASGS Edition 3, Non ABS Structures: Local Government Areas","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/non-abs-structures/local-government-areas","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Local government areas (2022 boundaries) (pow)","k":"ASGS local government area code (2022 boundaries), place of work","def":"A five-digit code, one digit for the state or territory and four for the area identifier, ending in zero. When an area is abolished its identifier is retired, and a new area takes the next available identifier in alphabetical order, so codes are not reused across vintages.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, ASGS Edition 3, Non ABS Structures: Local Government Areas","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/non-abs-structures/local-government-areas","lim":"It is not a second, independent measurement: POWLGA and this column come from the same workplace address, so differences between them are boundary changes and never commuting behaviour. Mesh blocks are \"the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS\" and are designed to hold between 30 and 60 dwellings. This is finer than anything the published Census reaches: the dictionary states that destination zones \"are aggregates of whole Mesh blocks (though data is not coded to the Mesh block level)\", so a mesh block on this column comes from the address geocoding inside the integrated asset rather than from the published place-of-work coding chain. Compared against MBUCP it gives commuting origin and destination at the finest ASGS unit.","dsrc":"ABS, ASGS Edition 3, Main Structure and Greater Capital City Statistical Areas: Mesh Blocks","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/mesh-blocks","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Meshblock (pow)","k":"ASGS mesh block code, place of work","def":"An 11-digit code, one digit for the state or territory and ten for the mesh block, drawn from the 368,286 mesh blocks in ASGS Edition 3. SA2s are \"medium-sized general purpose areas\" whose \"purpose is to represent a community that interacts together socially and economically\", generally holding 3,000 to 25,000 people. The ABS builds SA3s \"from whole Statistical Areas Level 2\" and designs them \"for the output of regional data\", clustering SA2s with similar regional characteristics into areas of roughly 30,000 to 130,000 people. The ABS states that \"SA4 boundaries represent labour markets\" and that they are \"designed with an emphasis on stability over time to support the time series of statistical releases such as the Quarterly Labour Force publication\". That makes this the column to use when Census place of work has to be compared with Labour Force Survey estimates, and SA4UCP is the matching residential region.","dsrc":"ABS, ASGS Edition 3, Main Structure: Statistical Area Level 4","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/statistical-area-level-4","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Sa4 (pow)","k":"ASGS Statistical Area Level 4 code, place of work","def":"A three-digit hierarchical code: one digit for the state or territory and two for the SA4, as in 102 for Central Coast. The ABS notes that these boundaries are \"a cartographic representation of legally designated boundaries and therefore should not be used for legal purposes\", and that Jervis Bay, Christmas Island, the Cocos (Keeling) Islands and Norfolk Island are grouped together as Other Territories. Against STEUCP, the state of usual residence, it identifies cross-border workers, which matters most around Albury-Wodonga, Tweed Heads-Coolangatta and the ACT boundary.","dsrc":"ABS, ASGS Edition 3, Main Structure: Australia and State/Territory","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/australia-and-stateterritory","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"State (pow)","k":"ASGS state and territory code, place of work","def":"A single digit: 1 New South Wales, 2 Victoria, 3 Queensland, 4 South Australia, 5 Western Australia, 6 Tasmania, 7 Northern Territory, 8 Australian Capital Territory and 9 Other Territories.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, ASGS Edition 3, Main Structure: Australia and State/Territory","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/main-structure-and-greater-capital-city-statistical-areas/australia-and-stateterritory","lim":"Cross-border commuting is the only movement it can show, so it is close to useless as a mobility measure for the great majority of workers whose job is in their own state. The ABS defines it as recording \"the geographic area in which a person usually lived one year before the Census\" and states that \"the base area that is output is Statistical area level 2\". In this dataset it sits with MBU1P, LGAU1P and STEU1P, which carry the same one-year-ago address at mesh block, council and state level, so this column is the standard-output version of that address.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence one year ago (PUR1P)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-usual-residence-one-year-ago-pur1p","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Place of Usual Residence One Year Ago","t":"categorical","k":"Place of usual residence one year ago, ASGS area code","def":"An ASGS area code, output at Statistical Area Level 2 and aggregable upwards, with four-digit special purpose codes for cases that cannot be placed: 9099 capital city not further defined, 9299 overseas, 9499 no usual address, 9799 migratory, offshore and shipping, 9899 state or territory not further defined, &&&& not stated and @@@@ not applicable.","p":"2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence one year ago (PUR1P)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-usual-residence-one-year-ago-pur1p","lim":"The overseas category is a single code with no country attached, so a return migrant cannot be traced to an origin, and 'capital city not further defined' and 'state not further defined' mark answers too vague to place rather than real locations. Children under five are not applicable, so any migration rate calculated on the whole population will be diluted unless that group is removed.","where":["madip-ge-030101d-census2016-census2016person-2016 / census_2016_person","madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"],"dom":129},{"n":"QALFP","d":"What subject the person's highest completed post-school qualification was in.","full":"What subject the person's highest completed post-school qualification was in. The ABS defines the variable as describing \"the field of study of a person's highest completed non-school qualification\", coded using the Australian Standard Classification of Education (ASCED), 2001. QALLP on the same row holds the level of that same qualification, so field and level have to be read together: a certificate III in engineering and a doctorate in engineering share this code.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Non-school qualification: field of study (QALFP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/non-school-qualification-field-study-qalfp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Non-School Qualification: Field of Study","t":"categorical","k":"ASCED 2001 field of study code","def":"A six-digit ASCED code nesting inside a four-digit narrow field and a two-digit broad field, giving 16 broad fields, 87 narrow fields and 435 detailed fields, with 'nfd' codes where the answer supports only a broader level and @@@@@@ for not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Non-school qualification: field of study (QALFP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/non-school-qualification-field-study-qalfp","lim":"It cannot be used to count qualification holders. The ABS warns that people who said they held a qualification but did not name a field are coded to not stated here, so the population that actually holds a qualification is not identifiable from this column alone. The 12.3 per cent non-response rate in 2021 falls to 2.3 per cent once the qualification indicator question is used as a filter.","where":["madip-ge-030101d-census2016-census2016person-2016 / census_2016_person","madipge-cen11-d-person-2011 / census_2011_person","madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"],"dom":130},{"n":"QALLP","d":"The level of the highest non-school qualification a person has completed, recorded as a level rather than a subject.","full":"The level of the highest non-school qualification a person has completed, recorded as a level rather than a subject. ABS defines it as a variable that \"describes the level of a person's highest completed non-school qualification\", coded to the Australian Standard Classification of Education (ASCED) 2001 Level of Education classification. QALFP on the same person record holds the field of study of that same qualification, and HEAP combines school and non-school attainment into one ranking. A person with several qualifications is counted once, at the highest level only.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Non-school qualification: level of education (QALLP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/non-school-qualification-level-education-qallp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Non-School Qualification: Level of Education","t":"categorical","k":"ASCED level of education (non-school qualification)","def":"A hierarchical ASCED level code running from postgraduate degree through graduate diploma and certificate, bachelor degree, advanced diploma and diploma, down to certificate levels I to IV, published at broad and detailed levels. The not applicable code pools four different situations — no non-school qualification, a qualification out of scope of ASCED, still studying, and aged under 15 — so it is not evidence that a person holds no qualification. Because only the highest level is kept, a tradesperson who later took a degree shows as a graduate with no trade.","where":["madip-ge-030101d-census2016-census2016person-2016 / census_2016_person","madipge-cen11-d-person-2011 / census_2011_person","madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"],"dom":131},{"n":"RAD","d":"The remoteness class of the place where the dwelling was counted, on the 2021 dwelling record.","full":"The remoteness class of the place where the dwelling was counted, on the 2021 dwelling record. Remoteness Areas group whole SA1s by their average ARIA+ score, a measure of road distance to service centres, and ABS states that they are \"identifiable by a 2 digit hierarchical code, comprising the 1-digit State and Territory, and a Remoteness Area identifier\". RAD is that state-based form; RAND on the same row is the national form of the same classification. Every person counted in the dwelling shares this value, and the person record's RANP is the usual-residence counterpart.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Remoteness Areas","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/remoteness-structure/remoteness-areas","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Remoteness areas (en)","k":"ASGS Remoteness Area code (state-based)","def":"A two-digit ASGS Edition 3 code: one digit for state or territory, one for the remoteness class. It is also where the dwelling is, not where its occupants usually live.","where":["madipge-cen21-d-dwelling-2021 / census_2021_dwelling"]},{"n":"RAID","d":"Whether the household counted in this dwelling paid more than 30 per cent of its income in rent.","full":"Whether the household counted in this dwelling paid more than 30 per cent of its income in rent. ABS allocates \"an in scope household to one of two categories: rent payments less than or equal to 30% of household income\" or more than 30 per cent, dividing weekly rent from RNTD by an imputed household income. Because the Census collects personal income in ranges rather than dollars, the denominator is built by assigning each member aged 15 and over a median dollar value for their INCP bracket, taken from the Survey of Income and Housing, and summing them. Only rented occupied private dwellings are in scope.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Rent affordability indicator (RAID)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/rent-affordability-indicator-raid","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Rent affordability indicator","t":"categorical","k":"Rent affordability category (30 per cent of household income)","def":"Four categories: rent payments 30 per cent or less of household income, rent payments more than 30 per cent, unable to be determined, and not applicable. The last covers unoccupied dwellings, owner-occupied dwellings and non-private dwellings.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Rent affordability indicator (RAID)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/rent-affordability-indicator-raid","lim":"It is not a measure of housing stress. The 30 per cent line is applied to every renting household regardless of income, so a well-off household paying a large rent by choice scores the same as a low-income household with no alternative; the usual stress measure restricts the rule to the bottom 40 per cent of incomes. The denominator is imputed from income brackets, so a household near a bracket edge can fall on the wrong side of the line.","where":["madipge-cen21-d-dwelling-2021 / census_2021_dwelling"],"dom":132},{"n":"RAND","d":"The remoteness class of the dwelling's location on a single national scale, without the state prefix that RAD carries.","full":"The remoteness class of the dwelling's location on a single national scale, without the state prefix that RAD carries. ABS defines the classification as one that \"divides the States and Territories into 5 classes of remoteness based on relative access to services\", and in its state-based form a remoteness identifier is only unique once a state digit precedes it, so the national form is what you need to treat Outer Regional Australia as one group across the country. RAD and RAND sit on the same 2021 dwelling record and describe the same place; they differ only in whether the state is part of the code. RANP is the person-level, usual-residence equivalent.","dsrc":"ABS Census geography glossary, Remoteness Areas (RA)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/geography/census-geography-glossary","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Remoteness areas (national) (en)","k":"ASGS Remoteness Area class (national)","def":"The five national remoteness classes — Major Cities of Australia, Inner Regional, Outer Regional, Remote and Very Remote Australia — under ASGS Edition 3, plus supplementary categories for migratory-offshore-shipping and no usual address.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census geography glossary, Remoteness Areas (RA)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/geography/census-geography-glossary","lim":"It cannot be broken down by state without joining to another geography column, which is what RAD is for. ABS defines the classification as dividing \"the States and Territories into 5 classes of remoteness based on relative access to services\", built by grouping SA1s on their average ARIA+ score. Because this is coded to usual residence rather than to where the person was counted, it can differ from RAND on the dwelling record for anyone away from home on Census night. It is the column to use when comparing remoteness across the whole country on one scale.","dsrc":"ABS Census geography glossary, Remoteness Areas (RA)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/geography/census-geography-glossary","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Remoteness areas (national) (ur)","k":"ASGS Remoteness Area class (national)","def":"The five national classes — Major Cities of Australia, Inner Regional, Outer Regional, Remote and Very Remote Australia — under ASGS Edition 3, with supplementary categories for migratory-offshore-shipping and no usual address.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census geography glossary, Remoteness Areas (RA)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/geography/census-geography-glossary","lim":"Remoteness is about distance to services, so it is not a measure of disadvantage and should not be used as one: some of the most disadvantaged areas in Australia sit inside Major Cities. Remoteness Areas are made up of SA1s grouped on their average ARIA+ score, and ABS states they are \"identifiable by a 2 digit hierarchical code, comprising the 1-digit State and Territory, and a Remoteness Area identifier\". The 2016 value uses the ASGS boundaries of that Census and the 2021 value uses ASGS Edition 3, so the two are not a clean before-and-after pair for the same person. In 2021 the person record also carries RANP, the same classification without the state prefix.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Remoteness Areas","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/remoteness-structure/remoteness-areas","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Remoteness area","k":"ASGS Remoteness Area code","def":"A two-digit ASGS code combining state or territory with the remoteness class, over five classes from Major Cities of Australia to Very Remote Australia, plus supplementary codes for migratory-offshore-shipping and no usual address.","p":"2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, Remoteness Areas","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/remoteness-structure/remoteness-areas","lim":"A change in this code between the 2016 and 2021 person records is not proof that the person moved: ARIA+ scores and SA1 boundaries are both rebuilt between editions, so an unmoved household can change class.
