It sits with SA1UCD, SA2UCD, SA3UCD and SA4UCD, described in the 2011 and 2016 metadata as the SA1 to SA4 'of dwelling address', and in 2021 with MBUCD, GCCSAD, SUAD, UCLD and TRD, all carrying the '(en)' tag for place of enumeration, which the Census glossary defines as \"the place at which the person is counted on Census Night, which may not be where they usually live\". Because a dwelling does not move, its enumeration state and the state it stands in are the same thing; the distinction only bites on the person table, where STEUCP is usual residence instead.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021 glossary, Place of enumeration","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/glossary/p","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"State of Dwelling on Census Night","k":"ASGS state and territory of enumeration for the dwelling","def":"A single ASGS state and territory code, the top level of the hierarchy that runs Mesh Block to SA1 to SA2 to SA3 to SA4 to state and territory, together with the Other Territories category and the migratory, off-shore and shipping category.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021 glossary, Place of enumeration","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/glossary/p","lim":"It is not where the household usually lives. A holiday house occupied on Census Night by a Victorian family is a New South Wales record here, so any count built on this column is a de facto count: the ABS reports East Pilbara with 39,529 people enumerated against 25,443 usual residents, and Rockingham with 131,213 enumerated against 135,678 usual residents.","where":["madip-ge-030103d-census2016-census2016dwelling-2016 / census_2016_dwelling","madipge-cen11-d-dwelling-2011 / census_2011_dwelling","madipge-cen21-d-dwelling-2021 / census_2021_dwelling"]},{"n":"STEUCP","d":"The state or territory a person usually lives in, which is the state-level roll-up of the mesh block their usual address was coded to.","full":"The state or territory a person usually lives in, which is the state-level roll-up of the mesh block their usual address was coded to. The Census Dictionary defines the underlying variable as recording \"the geographic area in which a person usually lives. It may or may not be the place where the person was counted on Census Night\", so this column follows the person home rather than staying with the dwelling they were enumerated in. UAICP on the same row says whether the person was at home that night, IFPURP says whether the address was imputed, and SA1UCP through SA4UCP hold the finer cuts of the same address.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence (PURP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-usual-residence-purp","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"State/territory of usual address","k":"ASGS state and territory of usual residence","def":"A single ASGS state and territory code derived from the mesh block the usual address was coded to, plus an overseas visitor category and the migratory, off-shore and shipping category. People with no fixed address write 'None' and are placed in a designated SA1 and SA2 for their state or territory.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of usual residence (PURP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-usual-residence-purp","lim":"A value here can be imputed rather than reported. Where the address was incomplete the ABS imputes place of usual residence, sometimes at a level coarser than mesh block, and IFPURP is the only column that records that this happened; non-response was 4.3% at SA2 level in 2021. The column also has nothing to say about how long the person has lived there, which is what UAI1P and UAI5P are for.","where":["madip-ge-030101d-census2016-census2016person-2016 / census_2016_person","madipge-cen11-d-person-2011 / census_2011_person","madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"]},{"n":"STEWKADP","d":"The state or territory a person worked in during the week before Census Night, held only on the 2011 person table.","full":"The state or territory a person worked in during the week before Census Night, held only on the 2011 person table. The ABS defines the underlying place-of-work variable as recording \"the geographic area in which a person worked in the week before Census Night\", with \"the address of the person's workplace ... coded to a Destination zone (DZN)\", and this column is that coding aggregated to state. Compared with STEUCP, the state of usual residence, it is what identifies cross-border commuters; the 2021 table replaces it with an explicit POWSTE alongside POWMB, POWSA2 and POWDZN.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of work (POWP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-work-powp","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"State/territory of workplace","k":"ASGS state and territory of place of work","def":"A single ASGS state and territory code, taken from the destination zone the reported workplace address was coded to, with separate categories for workplaces that could not be coded to a zone and for people the variable does not apply to.","p":"2011","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Place of work (POWP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/place-work-powp","lim":"A missing value is usually not a missing workplace: the variable applies only to employed people aged 15 and over, so the unemployed, people not in the labour force and people with unstated labour force status are all not applicable. It also describes one job in one week, so a second job in another state and any travel the job involves are invisible, and an employee working from home is coded to the employer's address, because the form asks for the employer's workplace address rather than where the work was done.","where":["madipge-cen11-d-person-2011 / census_2011_person"]},{"n":"STRD","d":"What kind of building the dwelling is: a separate house, a semi-detached or terrace house by storeys, a flat or apartment banded by the height of the block it sits in, a caravan, a cabin or houseboat, or an improvised home.","full":"What kind of building the dwelling is: a separate house, a semi-detached or terrace house by storeys, a flat or apartment banded by the height of the block it sits in, a caravan, a cabin or houseboat, or an improvised home. The ABS says the variable \"records the structure of private dwellings\" and that it \"is not collected from a question on the Census form\" — it comes from the ABS Address Register supplemented by Building Approvals, with field officers updating it during collection. It applies to private dwellings only, so every hotel, hospital, prison and nursing home is not applicable and NPDD and DWTD are the columns that describe those instead.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Dwelling structure (STRD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/dwelling-structure-strd","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Dwelling Structure","t":"categorical","k":"Census dwelling structure classification","def":"Twelve substantive categories covering separate house, two semi-detached bands, four flat and apartment bands set by the number of storeys in the block, a flat or apartment attached to a house, caravan, cabin or houseboat, improvised home or tent, and house or flat attached to a shop or office, plus not stated and not applicable, for fourteen codes in all.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Dwelling structure (STRD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/housing/dwelling-structure-strd","lim":"It says nothing about the size of the dwelling or who lives in it, and the flat categories count storeys in the block rather than the dwelling's own floor, so a ground-floor unit and a top-floor unit in the same nine-storey tower share a code. The not-attending code sits in the same column as the two student codes, which makes this single field both the student filter and the study-load grading; TYPP names the type of institution and TYSTAP combines the two with age. It applies to all persons, so a preschooler and a doctoral candidate are both in scope.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Full-time/part-time student status (STUP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/full-timepart-time-student-status-stup","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Full-Time/Part-Time Student Status","t":"categorical","k":"Census full-time or part-time student status","def":"Single-character codes: 1 not attending, 2 full-time student, 3 part-time student, 4 institution stated but full-time or part-time status not stated, & both institution and status not stated, and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Full-time/part-time student status (STUP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/full-timepart-time-student-status-stup","lim":"Full time and part time are the institution's own enrolment labels as the respondent understood them, not a measured study load, and the Census sets no hours threshold, so the split is not comparable with a workload definition. The ABS defines the classification as areas that \"represent Urban Centres, or groups of Urban Centres, that contain population of 10,000 persons or more\", built from SA2s, so this column places a dwelling in a town or city by name rather than inside an administrative boundary. It is one of the '(en)' enumeration geography columns beside UCLD, TRD, SOSD, GCCSAD and LGAD, all coded from the dwelling's address. A dwelling outside every significant urban area takes a state-specific 'not in a Significant Urban Area' code rather than a blank.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Significant Urban Areas","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/significant-urban-areas-urban-centres-and-localities-section-state/significant-urban-areas","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Significant urban areas (en)","k":"ASGS Significant Urban Area of the dwelling","def":"A unique four-digit non-hierarchical code, the first digit identifying the state or territory and the remaining three assigned alphabetically within it from 001. Because it is assembled from whole SA2s, its boundary only approximates the urban centre underneath it and includes surrounding non-urban land, and a cross-border area is coded to the state holding its largest urban centre, so Gold Coast – Tweed Heads dwellings in New South Wales carry a Queensland first digit.","where":["madipge-cen21-d-dwelling-2021 / census_2021_dwelling"]},{"n":"SUAP","d":"The named urban area of 10,000 people or more that a person usually lives in, on the 2021 person table.","full":"The named urban area of 10,000 people or more that a person usually lives in, on the 2021 person table. The ABS defines the classification as areas that \"represent Urban Centres, or groups of Urban Centres, that contain population of 10,000 persons or more\". The '(ur)' tag on this column, against '(en)' on SUAD, is the whole difference between them: SUAP follows the person to their usual address while SUAD stays with the dwelling they were counted in, so a person away from home on Census Night has different values in the two tables. It is not asked on the form: it is assembled from age, dwelling type, household composition, industry of employment, relationship in household and place of usual residence, and it has only two values, so its job is to define a denominator rather than to describe a person.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Level of workforce participation survey comparison flag (SVFP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/national-reporting-indicators/level-workforce-participation-survey-comparison-flag-svfp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Level of workplace participation survey comparison flag","t":"categorical","k":"Census national reporting scope flag","def":"Two categories: 1 for a person in scope of the workforce participation survey comparison population, and @ for not applicable. On the 2011 person table it sits with IFAGEP, IFMSTP and IFPURP, the matching flags for age, registered marital status and place of usual residence, so the imputed content of a record can be counted before any analysis leans on it.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Imputation flag for sex (IFSEXP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/imputation-flag-sex-ifsexp","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Imputation flag for SEXP","k":"Census imputation flag for sex","def":"Two codes, one meaning sex was not imputed and one meaning it was; the 2021 equivalent uses 01 and 02. It appears on all three 2016 tables and on the 2021 person table, which is what lets a person be tied to the family and dwelling they were counted in; DWELLING_ID and FAMILY_ID are the keys for those units themselves. It is not the PLIDA spine identifier, so it does not by itself reach a person's tax, health or payment records — ABS says the \"Person Linkage Spine allows us to link datasets through a spine of key information, separate from the main body of data\", and that link is what crosses datasets. The 2011 tables use C11_PERSON_ID for the same job.","dsrc":"ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/data-integration/integrated-data/person-level-integrated-data-asset-plida","dp":"ai","vp":"ai","od":"Synthetic id of individual person on dataset","k":"Synthetic person identifier within a Census file","def":"An opaque identifier with no internal structure, unique within one Census year's files. It applies to occupied private dwellings only, so unoccupied dwellings, non-private dwellings and migratory, off-shore and shipping areas are not applicable. The ABS says it \"combines Tenure type (TEND) and Landlord type (LLDD) to provide more detailed information for rented dwellings\", so it is built during processing rather than asked. Rent-free occupancy and life tenure schemes, which TEND keeps as separate codes, are folded into 'other tenure type' here, and shared equity purchases are folded into 'owned with a mortgage', so reading the two columns as nested loses those groups and will overstate mortgaged ownership.","where":["madip-ge-030103d-census2016-census2016dwelling-2016 / census_2016_dwelling","madipge-cen11-d-dwelling-2011 / census_2011_dwelling","madipge-cen21-d-dwelling-2021 / census_2021_dwelling"],"dom":153},{"n":"TISP","d":"How many children a woman aged 15 and over has ever given birth to, as a count rather than a band.","full":"How many children a woman aged 15 and over has ever given birth to, as a count rather than a band. The ABS defines it as recording \"the number of children ever born to each female aged 15 years and over\", and the question excludes adopted, foster and step children. It is the Census's lifetime fertility measure, so it counts children who have died or left home as well as those in the dwelling on Census Night. All numeric responses are accepted as reported.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Number of children ever born (TISP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/population/number-children-ever-born-tisp","lim":"It will not match the number of children present in the household, because it counts births over a lifetime and excludes adopted, foster and step children — HKIDP and the family variables describe who is actually there. It sits with SUAD, UCLD and the other '(en)' geography columns coded from the dwelling's address. Because this is the '(ur)' version it counts residents of a tourism region, which is what makes it useful for describing the workforce and population that a tourism economy rests on; TRD on the dwelling table is the enumeration counterpart.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Tourism Regions","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/non-abs-structures/tourism-regions","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Tourism regions (ur)","k":"ASGS Tourism Region of usual residence","def":"A five-character code combining a state or territory digit, the letter R and a three-digit region number, with 76 regions defined in ASGS Edition 3.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Tourism Regions","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/non-abs-structures/tourism-regions","lim":"It cannot measure tourism. The value comes from where the person lives, so a visitor counted in a region on Census Night still carries the region they usually live in, and Tourism Research Australia's own visitor surveys are what estimate flows. Coverage is also incomplete: Christmas Island, the Cocos (Keeling) Islands, Norfolk Island and Jervis Bay fall outside the structure, so an absent value there is a gap in the classification rather than a missing response.","where":["madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"]},{"n":"TYPP","d":"Which kind of institution a student was attending: preschool, primary or secondary split three ways by government, Catholic and other non-government, or tertiary split into vocational education including TAFE and university or other higher education.","full":"Which kind of institution a student was attending: preschool, primary or secondary split three ways by government, Catholic and other non-government, or tertiary split into vocational education including TAFE and university or other higher education. The ABS defines it as recording \"the type of education institution being attended by people who are full-time or part-time students\", collected from a mark box. Each of primary, secondary and tertiary also carries a not-further-defined code, used when a person named the broad type but not the sector. STUP on the same row says whether the attendance was full time or part time, and a person coded not attending there is not applicable here. Non-response was 0.8% in 2021, low because the question only reaches people who said they were students.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Type of educational institution attending (TYPP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/type-educational-institution-attending-typp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Type of Educational Institution Attending","t":"categorical","k":"Census type of educational institution attending","def":"Sixteen categories: preschool; three primary sectors plus primary not further defined; three secondary sectors plus secondary not further defined; tertiary split into vocational education including TAFE, university or other higher education, and tertiary not further defined; other; and not stated, not applicable and overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Type of educational institution attending (TYPP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/type-educational-institution-attending-typp","lim":"It names the institution, not the course or the level being studied, so a TAFE student doing a certificate II and one doing an advanced diploma share a code; QALLP holds the level of a completed non-school qualification and QALFP the field. The ABS says it \"combines responses from Type of educational institution attending (TYPP), Full-time/part-time student status (STUP) and Age (AGEP) to indicate a person's attendee status at an education institution\". It exists so that a common output cut — full-time university students aged 15 to 24, say — can be read from a single field instead of a three-way cross-tabulation. Its not-applicable code means the person was not attending an institution.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Educational institution: attendee status (TYSTAP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/educational-institution-attendee-status-tystap","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Educational Institution: Attendee Status","t":"categorical","k":"Census educational institution attendee status","def":"About thirty two-digit codes: 10 preschool, 21 to 29 primary by sector, 31 to 39 secondary by sector, 41 to 45, 51 to 55 and 61 to 65 for vocational, university and tertiary-not-further-defined broken by age and study mode, 71 to 73 other, plus && not stated, @@ not applicable and VV overseas visitor, thirty codes in all.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Educational institution: attendee status (TYSTAP)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/education-and-training/educational-institution-attendee-status-tystap","lim":"It cannot be decomposed cleanly, because the tertiary codes bundle an age band and a study mode into one value: recovering full-time status alone means mapping codes back rather than reading a field, and STUP is the direct column for that. The age bands inside it are fixed for output and cannot be recut, so AGEP is still needed for any other age analysis.","where":["madip-ge-030101d-census2016-census2016person-2016 / census_2016_person","madipge-cen11-d-person-2011 / census_2011_person","madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"],"dom":157},{"n":"UAI1P","d":"Whether a person's usual address a year before the Census was the same one they usually live at now, another Australian address, or an address overseas.","full":"Whether a person's usual address a year before the Census was the same one they usually live at now, another Australian address, or an address overseas. The ABS defines it as indicating whether a person \"lived in the same address one year ago as their current usual residence, lived elsewhere in Australia one year ago, [or] usually lived in another country one year ago\", from the question 'Where did the person usually live one year ago (at 10 August 2020)?'. STEU1P holds the state that goes with it and UAI5P asks the same question over five years. It applies to people aged one year and over, so infants are not applicable.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Usual address one year ago indicator (UAI1P)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/usual-address-one-year-ago-indicator-uai1p","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Usual Address One Year Ago Indicator","t":"categorical","k":"Census usual address one year ago indicator","def":"Six codes: 1 same address as at this Census, 2 elsewhere in Australia, 3 overseas one year earlier, & not stated, @ not applicable for people aged under one, and V overseas visitor.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Usual address one year ago indicator (UAI1P)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/usual-address-one-year-ago-indicator-uai1p","lim":"'Same address' means the same usual residence at two points, not that the person never moved: someone who moved out and back within the year reads identically to someone who stayed put. Where a child under 16 gave no answer the value can be copied from a parent's response, so an apparent child move is really the parent's, and the two records are not independent.","where":["madip-ge-030101d-census2016-census2016person-2016 / census_2016_person","madipge-cen11-d-person-2011 / census_2011_person","madipge-cen21-d-person-2021 / census_2021_person"],"dom":158},{"n":"UAI5P","d":"Whether a person's usual address five years before the Census was the same one they live at now, another Australian address, or an overseas one.","full":"Whether a person's usual address five years before the Census was the same one they live at now, another Australian address, or an overseas one. The ABS defines it as indicating whether a person \"lived in the same address five years ago as their current usual residence, lived elsewhere in Australia five years ago, [or] usually lived in another country five years ago\", asked as 'Where did the person usually live five years ago (at 10 August 2016)?'. It pairs with STEU5P, which holds the state, and with UAI1P for the shorter window. The ABS defines it as indicating \"whether a person was at home or elsewhere on Census Night\". This is the column that tells a reader when the enumeration geography and the usual-residence geography part company: where it reads 'elsewhere in Australia', the dwelling the person appears in is not the dwelling they live in, and the household composition around them is not their own. Non-response was 4.3% in 2021, and where usual residence was not stated both this variable and PURP are imputed.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Usual address indicator Census night (UAICP)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/location/usual-address-indicator-census-night-uaicp","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Usual Address Indicator Census Night","t":"categorical","k":"Census usual address indicator on Census Night","def":"Three published categories: 1 at home, 2 elsewhere in Australia, and V overseas visitor. The ABS says \"Urban Centres and Localities (UCLs) represent areas of concentrated urban development\" and are \"defined using Statistical Areas Level 1 (SA1s) that meet density and/or urban infrastructure criteria\", with urban centres needing 1,000 people or more and localities 200 to 999. It is the finest of the dwelling table's settlement geographies, sitting under SUAD and beside SOSD and SOSRD, which band the same classification into urban-rural groupings.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Urban Centres and Localities","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/significant-urban-areas-urban-centres-and-localities-section-state/urban-centres-and-localities","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Urban centres and localities (en)","k":"ASGS Urban Centre or Locality of the dwelling","def":"A six-digit hierarchical code built from the state or territory, the section of state, the section of state range and a UCL identifier, so Jervis Bay (L) is 9-2-2-002. SOSP and SOSRP on the same row are the coarse urban-rural cuts of this same classification, and SUAP is the 10,000-plus aggregation above it, so the three together let a person be placed on a settlement-size gradient rather than in an administrative area.","dsrc":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Urban Centres and Localities","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/significant-urban-areas-urban-centres-and-localities-section-state/urban-centres-and-localities","dp":"official","vp":"ai","od":"Urban centres and localities (ur)","k":"ASGS Urban Centre or Locality of usual residence","def":"A six-digit hierarchical code composed of state or territory, section of state, section of state range and a UCL identifier, with special codes for migratory, off-shore and shipping, no usual address, and outside Australia.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Urban Centres and Localities","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/standards/australian-statistical-geography-standard-asgs/edition-3-july-2021-june-2026/significant-urban-areas-urban-centres-and-localities-section-state/urban-centres-and-localities","lim":"Settlement size sits in the middle of the code rather than in the UCL identifier: the second and third digits are Section of State and Section of State Range, so a size comparison has to read those, or the SOSP and SOSRP columns, not the UCL name. It is the output form most Census tables use, and it inherits VEHD's exclusions of motorbikes, scooters and heavy vehicles.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Number of motor vehicles (ranges) (VEHRD)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/transport/number-motor-vehicles-ranges-vehrd","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Number of Motor Vehicles (ranges)","t":"categorical","k":"Banded count of motor vehicles at the dwelling","def":"Seven categories: 0 no motor vehicles, 1 one, 2 two, 3 three, 4 four or more motor vehicles, plus & not stated and @ not applicable.","p":"2011, 2016, 2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Number of motor vehicles (ranges) (VEHRD)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/transport/number-motor-vehicles-ranges-vehrd","lim":"The top band closes at four, so a four-car household and a fifteen-car one are indistinguishable and any mean vehicles-per-dwelling built from this column understates the true figure; VEHD keeps single values to 29 and is the column for that. It is derived by combining QALLP, the level of a completed non-school qualification, with TYPP, the type of institution being attended, so it holds no new answer of its own. The ABS says it \"is applicable to persons born overseas and records the year in ranges when they first arrived in Australia to live for one year or more\" and that it \"is derived from Year of arrival in Australia (YARP)\". It is a recode built during processing from HSCP, the highest year of school completed, and QALLP, the level of non-school qualification, rather than a question in its own right. It applies to people aged 15 and over.","dsrc":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Attainment of Year 12 or Certificate III or higher (YR12C3P)","durl":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/national-reporting-indicators/attainment-year-12-or-certificate-iii-or-higher-yr12c3p","dp":"official","vp":"official","od":"Attainment of year 12 or certificate iii or higher","t":"categorical","k":"Census Year 12 or Certificate III attainment flag","def":"Four categories: 1 attained Year 12 or equivalent or Certificate III or higher, 2 has not attained, @ not applicable, and V overseas visitor.","p":"2021","s":"sourced","src":"ABS Census Dictionary 2021, Attainment of Year 12 or Certificate III or higher (YR12C3P)","url":"https://www.abs.gov.au/census/guide-census-data/census-dictionary/2021/variables-topic/national-reporting-indicators/attainment-year-12-or-certificate-iii-or-higher-yr12c3p","lim":"It is nested inside YR12C2P — anyone coded 1 here is coded 1 there — so cross-tabulating the two produces an empty cell rather than new information, and the difference between them is the Certificate II group alone.
